comments.text: The 6510's data direction register for the port at $01. No part changes it: the start-up's clear loop ($7F30-$7F37) zeroes $02-$FF only, and the utility program's printer code, which nothing reaches (send_report $8602), would copy $00-$FF to $CA00 and write the same values back ($860E, $86A5), so it keeps the KERNAL's setting. Not code: no JMP, JSR, branch or vector in any part leads to $0000 (the RAM RESET vector at $FFFC holds $0000, but a reset brings the KERNAL ROM and its own vector back).

The 6510's processor port, the memory map: $35 in play (RAM, the I/O area at $D000, no BASIC or KERNAL ROM), $34 all RAM, so the RAM under $D000-$DFFF can be read and written. Written by all_ram_in ($25B8, $34, interrupts off), io_back_in ($2751, $35), irq_handler (saved at $294C, $35 at $2951, restored at $295F) and loader_main ($FF06-$FF88: $35 while it talks to the drive, $34 around each buffer access, the caller's value back at the end). The utility program's printer code sets $36 (KERNAL ROM in) to print through the KERNAL ($863B-$8695), but nothing reaches that code (send_report $8602).

Map column of the map window's left edge: the party's column $57 less $59 (9), so the party stands in the window's tenth column of $54 (19). Negative near the map's west edge (the game tests the columns it scans from it with BMI at $9562 and $AFA0). The game's moves change it (J: DEC at $AE4E, L: INC at $AE6D), switching parties sets it from the party table (+8, $9C2A-$9C31), an exit to another map sets it from the exit's square ($89F7, $8A1E), module 4 ($CBF8), the Ranger Center ($7ED1) and the utilities' Restart ($8172) set it; read by $0A87 (entry $043A, back to the party's column), $0B2D (a square's window column) and the game: its redraws ($AEA7, $AED1, $AF99), the encounter scan ($955B), the move checks ($AD5B, $AD93) and square_in_view ($B11B). Saved with the game (zero page $02-$0F at $F478).

Map row of the map window's top edge: the party's row $58 less $5A (4), so the party stands in the window's fifth row of nine. Negative near the map's north edge (BMI at $AF8E). The game's moves change it (I: DEC at $AE2F, K: INC at $AE8C), switching parties sets it from the party table (+9, $9C35-$9C3C), an exit to another map sets it from the exit's square ($89F9, $8A20), module 4 ($CC03), the Ranger Center ($7EDC) and the utilities' Restart ($8176) set it; read by $0A87 (entry $043A), $0B36 (a square's window line) and the game ($9546, $AD5D, $AD95, $AEAC, $AECC, $AF87, $B123). Saved with the game.

Low byte of a 32-bit count of elapsed game time: $04, $05, $06 and $F4FD, low first. Each step adds the map header's byte +$36 (game $AF61-$AF72, with the carries into $05, $06 and $F4FD). The start-up's 'N' (search every side for the last autosave) loads each side's save and keeps the one with the largest count (startup $8243-$8268), and the utilities' Start does the same ($81CF-$81F1); the game's countdown at $82B5 measures $F0 units from the count map 20's arm_self_destruct copies to $F4FA-$F4FC ($406B; its show_countdown reads it too, $408B); map 13's clone pods stamp it and measure from it ($3E27, $4258). Saved with the game; 0 to 255.

Second byte of the 32-bit elapsed-time count ($04-$06, $F4FD): incremented by the game when $04 carries ($AF6A), read by the countdown ($82C1), the start-up's and the utilities' searches for the latest save ($8247, $81D3), map 20's arm_self_destruct and show_countdown ($4070, $4094) and map 13's clone pods ($3E2C, $425F). Saved with the game.

Third byte of the 32-bit elapsed-time count ($04-$06, $F4FD): incremented when $05 carries ($AF6E), read by the countdown ($82C7), the start-up's and the utilities' searches ($824B, $81D7), map 20's arm_self_destruct ($4075) and map 13's clone pods ($3E31, $4267). Its own carry goes into $F4FD in the saved page. Saved with the game.

Number of members in the current party, 0-7: the positions 1-$07 of the party table at ($68) that hold a record. party_add adds one ($1753), remove_member takes one away ($1831), the game sets it when the party changes ($9C26, and the encounter scan's $94FF, from party_size_of $02AB) or a member joins or leaves ($999B, $A47C, $9B89; $9B54 takes back the one party_add adds when a member is copied into another party); Order, module 4, the Ranger Center ($7EC6) and map 13's release_clone ($42A8) write it too. Read wherever members are counted: the digit keys of the main loop ($7EAE), the roster ($15C9, $1655), pick_member ($178B), the divide and pool loops ($0E57, $15A1). Saved with the game.

Number of the current party, 0-3 (Disband splits the group into up to four parties; View switches between them). Picks the party table $F400 + 14*$08 (party_table_ptr, $1768) for select_member ($11F8), the roster ($15DA, $1637), party_add_current ($1746), find_party_of ($1798) and remove_member ($17FB). Written by the game ($94EA, $9521, $9527, $99B6, $9C21), module 4 ($CA73 and $CB09 while it walks the parties caught in the blast, $CBC6 after it) and the Ranger Center ($7EC1). Saved with the game.

Map or directory entry number: the current party's map in play (also kept at +10 of each party table, game $9C40), and the argument of the engine's directory routines: enter_map ($25BD, compared with $91, the map in memory), load_map_pages ($2608: bit 7 set means a substitute number from T35/L8 byte $80+), load_portrait, load_module and load_item_table (each saves it, uses it and puts it back: $2664/$2678, $26AA/$26B4, $26CD/$26D3), unpack_map_stream (which, like load_map_pages, stores the substitute for a negative number, $26FE, and ends with $09 = $91, $271F), unpack_entry ($2763) and load_dir_entry ($2841). The tile set number passes through it at $25F7. Saved with the game; 0 on the world map.

Number of character records in use, 0-7, all parties together: records 1-$0A at $F500-$FBFF. Raised when a character is created (Ranger Center, ranger $7F86) or joins (game $A47A) and when map 13's release_clone adds a clone ($42A6), lowered by remove_member ($1833). The game's main loop ends the game when it is 0, or when no record 1-$0A is alive ($7ED5-$7EFC): alive is conscious ($02C3), or unconscious (condition 0 from $0371, CON -1 to -10) with byte +$28, the afflictions, at 0 ($7EED-$7EF1). So a member who is unconscious and afflicted counts as lost, as do the seriously wounded and worse. The radio program ($7F05, $800D), the game ($9A12, $9BE2, $B1A8, $B542, $B7E2), module 4 ($CA18), maps 4 and 39 ($421B, $3C73), the Ranger Center ($7F73, $81FF) and the utilities ($8145, $85F6) loop over the records with it. Saved with the game.

Highest party number in use, 0-3: the number of parties less one (Disband splits the group). The roster header prints it plus one after the current party's number plus one (roster_draw $15E5); remove_member walks the party tables 0 to $0B ($1835); the game reads it when it switches or merges parties ($840E, $87E4, $94F6, $9917 ...), raises it when a runner splits off ($993D) or a member disbands ($9AD4) and lowers it after a merge ($99E2); module 4 ($CB05) and the Ranger Center ($7EBD) lower it when they delete a party. Saved with the game.

Fraction of a minute of the game clock (0-255): each step adds the map header's byte +$34 here, and the carry goes into the minutes $0D (game $AF32-$AF39). Saved with the game; apart from the copies of $02-$0F that save it and load it back (engine $18EC, startup $8353, utils $80F1), only the game reads and writes it.

Minutes of the game clock, 0-59: each step adds the map header's byte +$35 and the carry from $0C; at 60 it wraps and the hour $0E goes up (game $AF3B-$AF4B). Read by the game's clock display ($B16E). Saved with the game.

Hour of the game clock, 0-23 (wraps at 24, game $AF4B-$AF56). The engine's map square drawer ($0B80-$0B8A) shows squares of class 9, radiation (the game's handler for the class is square_radiation $82E0), as tile 8 at night, hours 0-5 and 18-23, and as their map tile otherwise; the game prints it as the clock's first two digits ($B15D); map 0's desert_heat takes its day check from 6:00 to 17:59 and its night check otherwise ($5074). Saved with the game; 1 in play-map.

Speed of the text window's smooth scroll, 0-6: indexes the step tables at $21D3/$21DA and the pause table $21E1 in newline ($20FD, $2141). While newline scrolls, it holds the step's pixel lines from $21DA instead ($214C; the speed is put back at $2157), which scroll_window_step reads ($216A, $21A3). While $A8 is set, CRSR down lowers and CRSR right raises it (speed_keys, $254A-$255B). The game keeps the player's value and substitutes its own for some texts ($914D-$915B sets it with $A8 = 1, $9144 puts both back). Saved with the game; 2 in play-map.

Track of a file's first sector, 1-35: byte 0 of a directory entry (read_dir_entry, $27D0), the input of load_program ($28B5) and read_sector_10_11 ($FD1B), used by load_dir_entry ($2848) and save_dir_entry ($2864). For a packed stream byte 0 is the start byte in the sector, which unpack_entry keeps ($276A) before it overwrites $10 with the stream's track ($2780). check_disk_side sets 35 for T35/L8 ($18A4); the game ($7F03, $8814), the start-up ($81F1, $8298), the radio program ($819B), the Ranger Center ($7EFA), the utilities ($8220) and module 3 ($CA1C) set it before loading a program, the start-up ($7FEF) and module 4 ($CCA9) before reading a picture's first sector. The utilities' disk copier keeps the track it is copying here, with the sector in $11 ($83CA-$8408).

Logical sector of a file's first sector: byte 1 of a directory entry (read_dir_entry, $27D5), the input of load_program ($28B3) and read_sector_10_11 ($FD19); load_dir_entry and save_dir_entry pass it as X ($2846, $2862). For a packed stream byte 1 counts the sectors to step down from the directory's base: unpack_entry steps and counts it to 0 ($2775-$277E), then stores the stream's sector ($2782). check_disk_side sets 8 ($18A0); the game, the start-up, the radio program, the Ranger Center, the utilities and modules 3 and 4 set it with $10, and the utilities' disk copier keeps the sector it is copying here ($83CF-$840A).

General pointer (with $13), low byte. Its main users: the bitmap address of a glyph, tile cell or line (bitmap_line_address $2390, next_cell $23A0, add_column $23AD, draw_glyph $2243), the scroll copies (the source in copy_cells $DD9D; in scroll_window_step the destination, once $2174 has moved the source line's address to $14), the record copied over by copy_character ($1726), the picture decoder ($067F), the map lookups map_class_at, map_number_row, action_record and map_tile_row ($095C-$09DC, $0B06-$0B18), run_menu_item's handler table ($1C5B), and a jump vector: JMP ($0012) at jump_via_12 ($1EFD) for item_effect ($145F) and the print dispatcher ($1F05-$1F36), and the game's JMP ($0012) at $AC69.

High byte of the general pointer at $12: the bitmap page ($2395, $23A4), the scroll copy's source page, stepped a page at a time by scroll_copy_row's patched INC/DEC ($DD97), the high byte of the vector for JMP ($0012).

Second pointer (with $15), low byte: the source of the text window's scroll copy (scroll_window_step $2176-$2191, which leaves the destination in $12) and the destination of the map window's (copy_cells and its step slots $DD9F-$DDC2, set by the game's $BEF7), and in draw_tile_cells the address of the tile's four colour bytes, $DC00 + tile*4 ($22EC-$231C; read at $2376, stepped at $237C/$237F). The tile's bitmap bytes are read through the operand at $2368/$2369 instead. Map code uses it too: the loot-bag refill of maps 13, 21, 33, 41 and 43 (and map 32's copy, which nothing runs) keeps the template bag's record address here (map 21: STA $14/$15 at $3CA4/$3CA8, LDA ($14),Y at $3CB4); the Ranger Center points it at a new character's item lists (give_items, $7FB2-$7FC9, $81AF).

High byte of the pointer at $14: the scroll copy's destination page, stepped by scroll_copy_row's patched INC/DEC at $DD99; the tile set page in draw_tile_cells ($22EE, $2321); the template bag's page in map code's loot-bag refill (see $14).

Record pointer (with $17), low byte: the result of record_address ($1B10: $45/$46 + A*$4C), most often an item's eight-byte record at $3108 + 8*A ($0BCD, used by item_skill_number $0DD5, item_class $144C, item_effect $1456, reload_weapon $129F); also skill_attr_ptr's entry in the skill table ($0C61) and the second string of strings_equal ($240C). Read as ($16),Y by the game ($928E, $95F7, $9EC7-$9EF1, $A89E, $AA27, $AA2C, $AC3E, $B0AF, $BC8C), modules 1 and 2 and the Ranger Center ($8354, $835B: its skill table, from point_at_skill $84ED).
High byte of the record pointer at $16 (record_address $1B12, skill_attr_ptr $0C67).

The key read_key ($2514) returned last: the code from $EC (ASCII with bit 7 set, from key_table) or 0 for none, stored at $252D and returned from there ($2537). menu_key handles it ($1BBF, $1BDF, $1C04), wait_listed_key compares the list with it ($1B2B), the game's main loop tests it against the member function keys ($7EBA), and the utilities' prompts return it as the key that ended the wait ($8292, $82D2). $19 and $1A after it are the game's scroll counters.

Used only by the game: character rows its map-window scrolls still have to copy, 16 for a sideways scroll ($BE29-$BE2B, $BE57-$BE59) and 13 for one up or down ($BEB1-$BEB3, set up by $BEAC), counted down after each row ($BE3D, $BE6D, $BE89, $BEA5). From the game part's use.

Used only by the game: the character row its map-window scroll copies into next, handed in Y to the row-address routines $BEEE/$BEF0 and $BF0F/$BF12 (which use $049F/$04B7 and screen_row_address $0502): rows 1 to 16 down the screen for the sideways scrolls ($BE2F, $BE5D), 1 to 13 for the up scroll ($BE79; the source two rows lower), 16 down to 4 for the down scroll ($BE93-$BEA4, the source two rows higher). From the game part's use.
Record offset of the attribute print_attributes is printing, $0E-$14 (ST, IQ, LK, SP, AGL, DEX, CHR), kept across the label print ($10FF-$110E). Only print_attributes uses it.

Low byte of the engine's 24-bit number $1C-$1E: an amount of cash (cash_load $14DE, cash_add $136B, cash_compare $0C1C, cash_spend_subtract $0C05), an experience total (exp_load $1571), a roll added to experience (skill_check $0C41, attribute_check $0D2D), the sum to divide (view_divide_cash $0E32-$0E65), and the input of binary_to_bcd ($2449) for the number printers (word_to_bcd $1C91 sets it from X:A). The game ($8E76, $90C8, $9495, $B33A), modules 0 and 1 and the radio program load it.
Middle byte of the 24-bit number at $1C-$1E (cash_load $14E3, cash_add $1373, binary_to_bcd $244E/$245B, word_to_bcd $1C93).
High byte of the 24-bit number at $1C-$1E (cash_load $14E8, cash_add $137B, binary_to_bcd $2454/$245D; word_to_bcd clears it, $1C97).
Lowest pair of the eight BCD digits binary_to_bcd makes from $1C-$1E ($243D clears, $246D adds): digits 1 and 0, read last by print_bcd_field ($1CC8).
BCD digits 3 and 2 of binary_to_bcd's result ($243F, $2474), read by print_bcd_field ($1CC3).
BCD digits 5 and 4 of binary_to_bcd's result ($2441, $247B), read by print_bcd_field ($1CBE).
Highest pair, BCD digits 7 and 6, of binary_to_bcd's result ($2443, $2482), read first by print_bcd_field ($1CB9).

Text cursor column, 0-39: where the next glyph is drawn (draw_glyph $2219, $224D). set_cursor writes it ($1EEC), draw_char_advance moves it on ($1F8C), newline puts it at the window's left edge ($212A), get_cursor ($22E5) and push_zp23/pull_zp23 ($2582, $2577) read and restore it with the window. Written by nearly every printing routine and by the game, modules, start-up, utils, the Ranger Center and the radio program before they print, and by map 13 before a line input ($42C7).

Text cursor row, 0-24 in character rows (the menu bar is row 23): set_cursor ($1EEE), newline ($2134, $215C), clear_window ($22B1-$22CA), draw_frame ($132B-$1342); draw_glyph turns it into the screen and bitmap addresses ($223E). Saved and restored with $23 and the window by push_zp23/pull_zp23.

Left column of the text window, inclusive: where newline returns the cursor ($2128) and where word wrap measures from (draw_buffered_line $200E-$2021, window_width $21C5). 14 for the text window (text_window_open: 13, the frame's column, at $12B2, then one more at $12C5), 1 for the picture window (0 at $12D4, then $12E3), 0 for the message area ($1E89, $1ECF), and the game ($AF0B, $B8DE), module 4, the start-up and utils set their own; 14 in play-map.

Right column of the text window, inclusive: glyphs past it are not drawn (draw_glyph $221B), word wrap breaks before it (buffer_char $1FF2, draw_buffered_line $2037), clear and invert stop there ($2282, $22A2). 38 for the text window ($12C7), 11 for the picture window ($12E7), 39 for full-width text: draw_frame ($130D), the Geiger gauge ($0AA6), the roster ($15F2, $1646), the side prompt ($18C9), the menu bar ($1B41, $1B68), the message area ($1E8D, $1ECB), the '(RETURN)' prompt ($21F0) and the disk error ($2811). Outside the engine the game's clock ($B14B), the start-up ($7F5C, $7F67), utils ($7FBE, $818F) and module 4 ($CCF7) set 39, and utils and module 4 set 36 inside their frames ($7E36, $CD17).

Top pixel line of the text window: where scroll_window_step starts moving lines up ($2164) and where clear_window starts ($22AC). 16 ($10) for the windows (window_clear $1302), the message area's own value for rows 18-22 ($1E81).

Bottom pixel line of the text window, exclusive: newline scrolls when the cursor would reach it ($212C), scroll_window_step stops there ($219F), clear_window clears up to it ($22C1). $70 for the windows (window_clear $1306, lines 16-111), $78 after draw_frame ($1311); module 4, the start-up and utils ($7E3E) set their own.

Reverse video: 0 normal, $FF reversed. EORed into each glyph byte (draw_glyph $225B) and each tile cell byte (draw_tile_cell $236A), and used by clear_or_invert ($2291). Text codes $01/$02 set and clear it (inverse_on $1FA6, inverse_off $1FA9); the roster ($1666) and the menu bar ($1B61) set it per item. $2A-$2B after it: no instruction in any part's listing names them; only the start-up's clearing of $02-$FF writes them ($7F34), apart from utils' copy of zero page in send_report, which never runs ($860E, $86A5).

Line input mode: non-zero accepts only digits ($1D4C-$1D56). input_line ($1D06) and input_line_x ($1D00) both store 0 ($1D09); only the digits-only entry $1CFD, which nothing calls, would store $FF. So in practice always 0 after a line input.

Leading-zero state of print_bcd_field: $FF until the first non-zero digit ($1CB3), during which a zero digit is replaced by the pad character $2E; cleared by the first non-zero digit or the last digit ($1CE9).

Character printed for a leading zero by print_bcd_digit ($1CE2): $20 (space) for the padded printers ($1CA1), 0 for the unpadded ones ($1CAF; character 0 is not printed, $1CF3). The game's clock pads the hour with character $5C, the frame's horizontal bar, since the clock sits in the top border, and the minutes with '0' ($B15B, $B16C); map 20's countdown pads its minutes with '0' too ($40DD).

Digit counter of print_bcd_field: 8 at the start ($1CB7), down to 1 ($1CFA); a digit is printed only when its position is not above the field width $30 ($1CEF), and the last position always prints a digit ($1CD6).

Width of a printed number, in digits (1-8): print_bcd_field prints only positions up to it, so a padded number is right-aligned in this many columns and longer numbers lose their leading digits. Set by the callers: 3 for the attributes ($10F3) and the skill levels ($11B0), 8 for the unpadded printers ($1CAB), 2 for the game's clock ($B14F); print_slot_number sets 1 ($1867), which the roster line raises to 2 for AC and AMM ($167C) and to 3 for MAX ($16B9). The game elsewhere ($9343, $B682, $BAB6, $BAD6), map 20's countdown ($40D6), modules 0, 1 and 2 and the Ranger Center set it too, and so does utils' print_report, which never runs.

Text pointer (with $32), low byte: the zero-terminated string being printed (print_string $1DE3, next_string_byte $1EF1), the buffer of a line input ($1D15-$1D9C), the menu text (menu_text_pointer $1BB7; find_menu_item, menu_key), the key list of wait_listed_key ($1B15), the first string of strings_equal ($240A), and the packed-text bit reader's position (text_start $28E7, text_bits $292E/$2930; find_message $1E29-$1E37). save_bit_pointer/restore_bit_pointer keep it ($2599, $25A6).
High byte of the text pointer at $31 (text_start $28ED, text_bits $2934, find_message $1E1A-$1E34, menu_text_pointer $1BBC).

Number of characters typed so far in input_line (0 up to $35): cleared at $1D13, raised for each key ($1D68), lowered by DEL ($1D75), the buffer index at which a key is stored and a deleted one blanked ($1D5A, $1D77), and used to trim trailing spaces at RETURN ($1D82-$1D8F).

Pixel line of the tile cell row draw_tile_cells is drawing: the tile's top line $37 ($230C), then 8 lower for the second row ($234B-$2350). Cells whose line is outside 8-$87 are skipped (the patched BIT/JMP at $2357, $2323-$2331).

Longest line input_line accepts ($1D5C), and the number of buffer bytes it clears first ($1D0E). Set by the callers: 13 for a name (ranger $836C, and map 13 for a clone's name, $42C3), 16 for the game's typed words ($892F).

Screen column of the tile draw_tile is drawing (its X, $22D8), read for both cell columns ($233A, $2345). The game sets it for its column redraws after a sideways scroll ($AE57-$AE7F: columns 2 and 0, or $22 and $24).

Top pixel line of the tile draw_tile is drawing (its Y, $22DA), copied to $34 ($230A). The game uses it as the line of a row redraw: $AEC6 draws a row of $54 squares at line $37 ($AE38-$AE41, $AE95-$AE9E, $AEF6-$AF07 for the whole window).

The count the text's plural switch (code $0A, filter_plural $206B, $2083) tests, 1 meaning singular, and which code $0F prints ($1F9D). set_count_one makes it 1 ($1EFA, entry $04DE); item_list_show sets it ($1083); the game sets it before texts about a number of things ($87C4, $AA86, $BAD2 and others), as do module 1 ($CCBE) and utils for its copy messages ($7F34-$8059). The radio program sets it to the points a character is given ($7EF8, $7FF2) and counts them down in it as they are spent ($801F-$80A9).

Selected item of the menu bar, from 0: ',' and '.' move it within 0-$3A with wrap-around, a letter or a hidden hot key selects one (menu_key $1BCF-$1C4D); find_menu_item turns it into a column ($1B91); run_menu_item runs it ($1C62). The game ($7E4D), Ranger Center ($7E3D) and utils ($7E57) start at 0; hidden items are numbered from $3A+1.

Number of the last item shown on the menu bar; items above it are the hidden hot keys after the bar's text (find_menu_item $1B93, menu_key $1BE6-$1C4F). 6 in the game (Use to Radio, $7E51), 1 on the title ($81A8); the Ranger Center and utils set theirs ($7E45, $7E5B).

Number of the current menu: picks the text (word $3B of the table at $3E, menu_text_pointer $1BB1) and the handler table (word $3B of the table at $40, run_menu_item $1C55). load_program sets 0 with its empty menu ($289A); the game, Ranger Center, title and utils set 0 for their own, and utils also shows menus 1-4 (its copy menu, $7F20; Reading. and Writing., $7FFD; Formatting., $7F60).
Column of the selected item's first letter on the menu bar, which is also its offset in the menu text (find_menu_item $1B8D/$1BAE); read by highlight_menu_item ($1B6D) and menu_key ($1BD9, $1BFB).
Screen row on which highlight_menu_item draws the selected item ($1B79): 23, the bottom line, set by the title ($81A4) and the Ranger Center ($7E41); nothing in the game changes it.

Address (with $3F) of the table of menu texts, one word per menu number: menu_text_pointer reads word $3B ($1BB5, $1BBA). load_program points it at its empty menu $28BD while a program loads ($2892); the game sets $7F3C (whose word 0 is the bar text $5BAB, $7E38), the title its table at $8368 ($8190), the Ranger Center and utils their own.
High byte of the menu texts table address at $3E (load_program $2896, game $7E3C).

Address (with $41) of the table of handler tables, one word per menu number: run_menu_item takes word $3B, then word $39 of that table, as the routine to call ($1C59-$1C6C). The game sets $7F3E ($7E40), whose word 0 is its handler table $7F18; the title, Ranger Center and utils set their own.
High byte of the handler tables address at $40 (game $7E44).

Screen row of a list's first line: 4 (list_page_setup $1A7C), read for the MORE line ($1A8D), the line labels ($1ABC) and the flashing of the chosen line ($1AEE). Order and the Ranger Center set their own ($CA79, ranger $8436).

Address (with $44) of the packed text block messages are taken from: $29E4, the engine's own (print_engine_msg $051B), the current map's (select_map_text $1E54, the word at ($61)), or one a program brings (game $7F5D, modules 0-2 and 4, the radio program, the Ranger Center, utils, the start-up). find_message reads it ($1E0F) and copies it to $52/$53; clear_message_area saves and restores it around its engine message ($1EC3, $1EE4).
High byte of the text block address at $43 (print_engine_msg $051F, select_map_text $1E59, find_message $1E13).

Base address (with $46) of the table record_address indexes ($1AFF: $16/$17 = $45/$46 + A*$4C): $3108 for the eight-byte item records ($0BCF), or a table of the game's own ($9EA9, the creature records at the map header's word +4) or the Ranger Center's ($84F7).
High byte of record_address's table base at $45 ($0BD3 sets $31, the game $9EAE and the Ranger Center $84FB their own).

Address (with $48) of a list's per-item routine, called through JMP ($0047) at call_list_item ($1968) for every line the list shows: print_item_row for the item list ($1087), print_skill_row for skills ($142B); the game (its loot and group lists, $9323, $B634), modules 1 and 2 and the Ranger Center ($840A) set their own. The routine prints the line or returns carry set to skip the item.
High byte of the per-item routine address at $47 ($108B, $142F).

Item chosen in a list: list_choose stores the item of the line whose digit was pressed ($19BB, from list_line_items $196B); item_list_show returns it ($109E), skill_reorder uses it ($13E5). list_show_page borrows it as a line counter while it clears the unused lines ($1A22-$1A2C). Module 2 and the Ranger Center set it to 1 before their skill lists ($CA57, $8406), and they and module 1 read the choice from it ($CAD0, $CB1F; $811B, $8151; $CC04).

Item shown on the first line of the list page: 1 for a new list (item_list_show $1081, skill_list_show $13FD; also the game's loot and group lists $931F, $B630, module 1 $CA57, module 2 $CA55 and the Ranger Center $8404), the item after the last one shown when paging forward ($19DB, wrapping to 1 at $4D), and the new top when paging back ($1A75). list_show_page offers items from it ($19F4).
Last item offered on the list page (list_show_page $1A35, list_page_back $1A5A): paging forward starts after it ($19D2).
Record size for record_address ($1B08): 8 for the item records ($0BD7), the game's own size for its table ($9EB2), the Ranger Center's for its own ($84FF).

One past the highest item number a list offers: item numbering wraps from it back to 1 ($19D5, $1A18, $1A6C). 31 for the 30 item slots ($107D); skill_list_show raises it once for each of the 31 skill pairs it scans, so 31 too ($13FA, $1401); the game ($9198-$9214, $B628), modules 1 ($CAE8, $CBDB) and 2 ($CB5B-$CB7C) and the Ranger Center (counted to 36, skills 1-35, $8414-$8416) set their own. The Order program only clears it ($CA8C): it calls list_line_label alone, which reads $25, $42, $50, $D0 and $D1, not this.

Number of items in the list plus one, by the engine's convention ($1066-$106F, $1416-$141D; game $9194-$9212, $B61F; module 2 $CB57-$CB76): list_fits_page compares it with the page length $4F ($19E3) to allow paging, and the MORE line appears when it is above $4F+1 ($1A97). item_reorder and skills_page read it ($100F, $13B1); the game lowers it as loot is taken ($92CE) and, before group_list_show, keeps the plain number of lines in reach in it ($B500, read at $B55A and $B59B). Module 1's list of goods for sale ($CBCC-$CBD7, the count from $CC5D) and the Ranger Center's skill list ($8410-$8428) store the count itself, without the one (module 1's other two lists keep the convention, $CAE3, $CB44): both tests then move by one, so such a list of exactly ten items can be paged but shows no MORE line. The Ranger Center's list never has ten: for a rolled IQ of 3-18 it holds 7, 9, 12, 16 or more skills (skill_table $8502). Whether a shop's list ever has exactly ten was not traced further.
Lines per list page: 9 (list_page_setup $1A80), the rows 4-12; list_show_page stops after it ($1A0B, $1A2F). The Ranger Center sets its own ($843A).

Line counter of the list page, 0-8: the line being filled (list_show_page $19F2-$1A20, list_page_back counts down from 8, $1A3F-$1A61), then the number of lines shown; a digit key must be below it ($19B1). list_line_label prints it plus one ($1AB9). Module 0 and Order use it for lists of their own.
Line (0-8) of the item chosen with a digit key ($19B5), which list_invert_line inverts when the choice flashes ($1AEB).

Address (with $53) of the packed text block being decoded, copied from $43/$44 by find_message ($1E11): its first bytes are the alphabet text_char looks codes up in (LDA ($52),Y at $2909), and text_start puts the bit reader $31/$32 at it plus $3C ($28E2-$28ED).
High byte of the decoder's text block address at $52 (find_message $1E15, text_start $28E9).

Number of map columns the map window shows: enter_map sets 19 ($25CF) and nothing changes it. The game counts its square loops with it ($9556, $AED6, $AF94 into the spare jump-table byte $0225) and square_in_view tests columns against it ($B11D); the window shows 9 rows ($AF82).

Number of rows of the current map, from the map header's byte +$2C (enter_map $25D5; the maps are square, so $56 gets the same value): 64 for the world map. Rows at or past it are off the map: the square drawer shows the header's border tile +$33 there ($0B49), the game tests it ($954F, $AF90); also the row count that locates the byte layer after the class layer ($0992).

Number of columns of the current map, header byte +$2C (enter_map $25D7): 64 for the world map, a power of two. Sets the row length of the map's layers: square classes, two to a byte, $56/2 bytes a row at $3400 ($0962-$097C), square bytes, $56 a row after them ($099E-$09B5), and tiles, $56 a row at $DE00 ($0B0C-$0B23); columns at or past it are off the map ($0B4D, game $9564, $AFA2).

Map column of the current party: $02 + $59, set after each move by $0A7F (entry $0437, $0A82), loaded from the party table (+8) when the party changes (game $9C2C) and stored back there ($9C47); the game also puts a new square in it before select_party stores it, for a party that moves in a fight ($A332) and for a runner ($994C). The distance routine at $08F5 measures from it ($090F); the game reads it for distances and events ($8347, $836C, $837A, $85B6, $8890, $89C1, $89E7, $997F, $AF2D, $B07C, $B105), and so does map 26's train ($4FA2). Module 4 and the Ranger Center set it ($CBF3, ranger $7ECC).

Map row of the current party: $03 + $5A ($0A84, entry $0437), loaded from the party table (+9, game $9C37) and stored back ($9C4D), and set by the game with $57 for a party that moves in a fight and for a runner ($A334, $9950); read by the distance routine ($08FA), the game ($834B, $8351, $835F, $8892, $89CB, $89E9, $9987, $AF2B, $B07E, $B107) and map 26's train ($4FA9). Module 4 and the Ranger Center set it ($CBFE, ranger $7ED7).

Column of the party inside the map window: 9 (enter_map $25DB), the middle of 19. The view's left edge is $57 - $59 (game $9C2F) and the party's column $02 + $59 ($0A8D); $0A96 (entry $0440) subtracts it ($0A98). Module 4 and the Ranger Center read it ($CBF6, ranger $7ECF).

Row of the party inside the map window: 4 (enter_map $25DF), the middle of 9 rows. The view's top edge is $58 - $5A (game $9C3A), the party's row $03 + $5A ($0A92); $0A9D subtracts it. Module 4 and the Ranger Center read it ($CC01, ranger $7EDA).

Pointer (with $5C) to row $63 of the current map's class layer at $3400: $56/2 bytes a row, two four-bit classes to a byte. $0953 (entry $0425) computes it when the row changes ($0976-$097C) and reads the class of square X (LDA ($5B),Y, $0982: low nibble for odd columns, high for even); $0A57 (entry $0431) writes a new class into it ($0A66-$0A7C).
High byte of the class-layer row pointer at $5B ($097C: $34 plus the row offset).

Pointer (with $5E) to row Y of the current map's byte layer, one byte per square after the class layer ($3C00 on the world map): $098E (entry $0422) sets it ($09AF) and $09F4 (entry $0443) reads the byte of column X from it ($09FC); $0A3D writes a new byte ($0A53). The game reads it too ($95B7). What the byte means is the game's business (an index into the header's tables, by its use with $09B8).
High byte of the byte-layer row pointer at $5D ($09B5).

Pointer (with $60) to a record of the current map: $09B8 (entry $0428) takes word Y of the map header's table list at +6 (a table's address) and then word A of that table ($09D9-$09DE). $0A00 (entry $042E) reads a square change from it ($0A07-$0A14) and the square drawer reads its byte 1 ($0B93). The game works through it all the time, reading and changing records ($82FF-$9354, $A42E, $B02D-$B0BF, $BE02-$BE1E), keeps it across run_action's table lookup and draw_view ($8855-$886D, $AC8F-$ACB2) and swaps it with $77/$78 ($BB61-$BB9C); modules 0-3 read their parameters through it. The own code of maps 0, 4, 5, 8, 11, 13, 21, 23-26, 32, 33, 35, 38-41, 43 and 49 reads records through it as well, and all of them but maps 5, 11, 24 and 39 write through it; maps 4, 8, 13, 21, 32, 33, 38, 40, 41, 43 and 49 keep it, point it at other records through $0428 and put it back.
High byte of the map record pointer at $5F ($09DE; the game keeps and restores both, $8855-$886D, $AC8F-$ACB2).

Address (with $62) of the current map's header: $4C00 for a 64x64 map, $3A00 for a smaller one, by the map's flag in T35/L8 (load_map_pages $2606-$261A; the low byte is always 0). Its first word is the map's text block (select_map_text $1E52); +6 on, the table list ($09BD); +$2C the size ($25D3); +$30 the tile set ($25EE); +$33 the border tile ($0B5E); +$34/+$35 time per step and +$36 the count per step (game $AF32-$AF64); the game also reads the monster names at word +2 ($9E78), the monster records at word +4 ($9EA7), the random-encounter bytes +$2F, +$31 and +$32 ($B017-$B047) and message numbers ($BCE5), and the own code of maps 6, 19, 20, 22, 27 and 43 changes +$2F, +$31 or +$32 through it. Module 4 changes it ($CC67-$CC75).
High byte of the map header address at $61: $4C or $3A (load_map_pages $2616); module 4 sets $CC for one call ($CC6B) and puts it back ($CC72).

Map row the class-layer row pointer $5B/$5C points at: $0953 recomputes the pointer only when asked for another row ($0956-$095A); enter_map sets $FF so the first lookup on a new map recomputes it ($25EA).

Class a square is changed to by $0A00 (entry $042E): the first byte of a change record at ($5F) ($0A11), or the saved $AD for record byte $FE ($0A2A); bit 7 set leaves the square as it is ($0A3D). The game sets it for its own square changes ($8788, $87A8, $B0C3) and module 4 ($CBD5); the game's encounter scan also keeps the class of the square it is looking at in it ($956E, read at $95B9).

Square byte that goes with $64: the change record's second byte ($0A16) or the saved $AE ($0A2E), written into the byte layer by $0A3D ($0A51-$0A53). Set by the game ($878A, $87A5, $B024) and module 4 ($CBD9).

Address (with $67) of the current character's 256-byte record: $F400 + record*256, records 1-7 at $F500-$FBFF, set by select_character ($1203, entry $0338; select_member $0335 first looks the record up in the party table). Every character routine reads it as ($66),Y: name +$00, cash +$15-$17, sex +$18, attributes +$0E-$14, CON +$1D/$1E, experience +$21-$23, rank +$24, skills +$80-$BB, items +$BD-$F8. Also borrowed as a plain page pointer by write_save_page ($1880), save_checksum ($1928) and scramble_save ($1953). The fields the other programs use are listed at $F500.
High byte of the current character's record address at $66: $F4 + the record number (select_character $1208), so $F5-$FB in play.

Address (with $69) of a party table: $F400, $F40E, $F41C or $F42A for party 0-3 (party_table_ptr $1768, entry $029F). A table is 14 bytes: +1 to +7 the record numbers of positions 1-7, +8/+9 the party's column and row, +10 its map (game $9C17-$9C55), +11/+12/+13 the column, row and map it last left by an exit (game $89BA-$89D7). Used by select_member ($11FF), party_add ($1751), party_size ($175B), party_has_record ($17BD) and remove_member ($1802-$1849); the game and Order rearrange the tables through it, module 4 and the Ranger Center read and change tables through it too ($CA7A-$CC8C; $7EA1-$7F24), utils' restart_command writes every party's square and map through it ($8157-$8163), map 13's release_clone writes a clone's record number into the party through it ($42AE), and map 33 reads other parties' maps and squares through it ($3E6B-$3E8E).
High byte of the party table address at $68: always $F4 (party_table_ptr $1775).

Non-zero while the roster occupies the bottom of the screen: roster_show sets 1 ($17CD), as does the start-up ($7F73); the game clears it when it draws the map full width ($AEF0, from $AC8C: at its start and when Space hides the roster, $7F32; Space with the roster hidden calls roster_show). The roster routines do nothing without it ($15A9, $15D5, $1632); show_message prints at the bottom only when it is 0 or after clearing ($1E70); the square position routine keeps squares out of the roster's rows while it is set ($0B3F), as does draw_other_parties ($AD3F), and restore_view_if_covered redraws the view when it or $B7 is set ($B112).

Disk side check_disk_side wants (1-4): set from A on entry ($1897), when A also goes, as a digit, into the 'INSERT SIDE n.' prompt ($189B); compared with the side byte of T35/L8 ($18BC), and stored again, unchanged, when they match ($18C0).

Bits left in the packed-text bit buffer $6E, less one: text_start sets $FF, empty ($28F1); when it is negative text_bits takes the next byte at ($31) and sets 7 ($2921-$2927), and counts it down per bit ($293E).

Capital-letter flag of the packed-text decoder: a code $1E shifts a 1 into bit 7 (ROR with carry set, $28F5); after the next character's lookup the flag moves to bit 6 (LSR, $290B) and, when set, a character $61-$FA is turned into a capital ($290D-$291A). text_char's CLC/ROR clears it again for the following character.
Bit buffer of the packed-text decoder: the current byte from ($31), shifted right one bit at a time into the five-bit code (text_bits $2936, $293B; lowest bit first).

Low byte of a 16-bit total (with $70) for the engine's checks: cleared by $078D, added to by $079D (a signed add held between 0 and $FFFF), compared with the target $71/$72 by $07EF. skill_roll_total puts roll + attribute + 4*level here ($0C6A on); the game uses the same routines for its own rolls ($871C, $909F-$90E6) and also stores into it directly: each initiative slot in turn while melee_pick_next looks for the highest ($8061-$806D), and 100, the limit melee_chance holds its chance to ($829A).
High byte of the check total at $6F ($0792, $07B1-$07B3, $07F5).

Low byte of the 16-bit target (with $72) a check must reach: cleared by $0795, added to by $07C6 (held between 0 and $FFFF); skill_check and attribute_check set 15 + 5 * difficulty ($0867). The game halves it for some rolls ($8458-$845A) and keeps its own targets here ($8534, $86AD); it also keeps in it the highest initiative melee_pick_next has found ($806F-$8084), the melee chance tested against a d100 ($8103, $81EE) and the damage monster_takes_damage deals ($AAC8; set at $A057 for explosives).
High byte of the check target at $71 ($079A, $07DA-$07DC).

Used only by module 1, the shop: byte 4 of the shop's map record ($CA41-$CA45). What the shop pays for an item is its price less the price shifted right this many times (sell_price $CCC7, LDX $73 at $CCCA, arithmetic at $CCD4-$CCF7): 1 pays half, 2 three quarters, 0 the full price. From module 1's use (its names).

Used only by module 1, the shop: byte 3 of the shop's map record ($CA3B-$CA3F), the same shift for what the shop charges (buy_price $CCCF, LDX $74 at $CCD2): 0 charges the full price, which every shop record holds. From module 1's use (its names).

Number of the item table file to have at $3100 (entry of the directory at T35/L15, 0-4): load_item_table loads it unless it equals $76 ($26BD-$26CB). Set by module 1 from its parameter (+6, $CA04, $CA39); 0 in play-map.

Number of the item table file now at $3100: set by load_item_table when it loads one, before the read ($26C3), and used by save_item_table to write the table back to its own file ($26DC). The start-up and utils lower it by one just before load_item_table ($828E, $8216), which forces the table to be read again.

Pointer (with $78), used only by the game: the map record (from $5F/$60) its event and encounter code is working on, most often the record of an encounter group's square, found from the group's column and row (group_square_record $BB75). From it the game reads the monster numbers and counts of the group's three lines (bytes 3, 5, 7 and 4, 6, 8: $BAE9, $BAE6) and byte 9: bit 0 the monsters are identified, so their names are shown ($9E5D), bit 1 peaceful ($9EF6), both changed once either side attacks ($ABC9, $ABD6), and bits 4-7 the NPC that can be hired there, in the map's list 17 ($ABC0, Hire $A3F1). Swapped with $5F/$60 around the engine's map routines ($BB5F-$BB9C) and read as ($77),Y at $8428-$8717, $87BB, $9425-$946C, $95C9-$962C, $97BA, $9C9C, $9E5F-$9EF8, $B65A-$BACE and $BC1B; the game also writes the lines through it, their monster numbers and counts rolled when its groups are placed ($942E, $943E) and the live counts, with type 0 for a line left empty, written back by group_write_back ($BA47, $BA59). From the game part's use.
High byte of the game's record pointer at $77 ($BB63, $BB89, $BB98).

Pointer (with $7A), used only by the game: an encounter group's record, $EE00 + 376*party + 94*group (the game's $BBC7, A = party, X = group), or one of the group's 30-byte lines at +4 + 30*line ($BB9F); see encounter_groups at $EE00. The group's column and row at ($79)+0/+1 are passed to the engine's square routines $042B/$042E ($BB68-$BB7E), read by the group pass when it plans a step ($84EA-$84F2) and rewritten when the group moves ($879E, $87A2). From the game part's use.
High byte of the game's record pointer at $79: $EE-$F3 ($BBCF, $BBB0).

Pointer (with $7C) to row Y of the current map's tile numbers, one byte per square, in the unpacked map stream at $DE00 ($DE00 + Y * $56: $0B06-$0B23). The square drawer reads the tile there with the I/O banked out ($0BA3-$0BAB).
High byte of the tile row pointer at $7B: $DE plus the row offset ($0B21-$0B23).

Reach of the member acting, in feet (the unit of the distance table at $0921, 10 a square), used only by the game: member_reach ($BC39-$BC66) sets 0 for a member who is not conscious, 15 for melee (the eight squares around are 10 or 14 feet away), $FE for a weapon of a ranged class with rounds in it ($0413); weapon_use_rounds drops it to 15 for an empty or jammed gun ($BCBB-$BCBD), which weapon_damage_roll then swings as a club ($A801-$A805); choose_hire and encounter_portrait set $FF, any distance ($B6EE, $B920). group_in_reach compares a group's distance with it ($B6AE), and an NPC's attack choice tells melee from ranged by comparing it with $10 ($B50B). From the game part's use (its names).

Class of the weapon in use (item_class, entry $0365), used by the game only: set at $A54E and per member before an attack ($BC4E; 1 when the weapon fails $0413, $BC5F); compared with 13, the explosives, at $A024, $A048, $A56F, $A5D8, $AAAC and $AB22. From the game part's use. After it, $80-$87 are the Order program's copy of party table bytes 0-7, the old marching order, emptied as members are picked (order $CA08-$CA6F); $7F and $88: no instruction in any part's listing names them; only the start-up's clearing of $02-$FF writes them ($7F34), apart from utils' copy of zero page in send_report, which never runs ($860E, $86A5).

Pointer (with $8A), used only by the game: party A's order table, the first eight bytes of its block in party_orders ($F438 + 16 * party; order_tables_ptr $BCC0), one byte per party position 1-$07: the combat order chosen for the round, the index of its key in the game's order_keys ($B4BD, space H A W R E L U S): 0 none, 1 Hire, 2 Attack, 3 Weapon, 4 Run, 5 Evade, 6 Load/Unjam, 7 Use, 8 the party's Run. The space key shows the map and asks again ($B489); S, not named in the prompt, is Attack with the group list: its index 8, stored at $B449 like any key's, is replaced by 2 at once (choose_attack_listed $B4A0 goes back to $B443); apart from that, 8 is stored only by set_party_move_orders ($B3C7), for every member when Run is answered P)arty ($B461-$B469). get_party_orders clears it ($B3BB), orders_member_loop stores the key's index ($B449); resolve_orders runs each order's handler from the table at $9F2E ($9EFD-$9F0F), party_ranged_attacks ($9F82) and melee_round ($8026, $808A, $81CF) read it, the shot at a member tests it for Evade ($9E0A), and resolve_runs_and_moves tests it for 8 and 4 and clears it ($A293-$A2B8); also written at $8092, $A36E and $A53D and read at $B26C. From the game part's use (its names).
High byte of the game's pointer at $89: $F4 ($BCCB-$BCCD).

Pointer (with $8C), used only by the game: $89 + 8, the second eight bytes of the party's block in party_orders ($BCCF-$BCDA): each member's order parameter, the result of the order's handler (orders_member_loop $B46F; $B3CE-$B3D4 for the party's Run): for Attack the target line 0-47 with the fire mode in bits 6-7 ($A535, $A5F8), for Hire the line to hire from, for Weapon the item slot ($A264), for Run and the party's Run the direction 0-4 ($A2A9), for Use the Use dialog's kind * 16 + its X, the direction 0-4 or the patient's record number (choose_use $B76E-$B77C; what is used goes to use_order_choice $5BDB). From the game part's use (its names).
High byte of the game's pointer at $8B: $F4 ($BCD8-$BCDA).

Map number, used only by the game: the map a fight or an encounter scan is on (the game's 'battle map'). for_each_battle_party ($9F40) visits every party whose table names this map (+10), selects it and calls the routine at ($8E) ($9F48-$9F58). The game copies $09 in before its call at $94CF ($B197-$B19B; $AC9E-$ACA9 keeps the old value around it) and for each party of an encounter round ($B201-$B203), and reads it elsewhere ($83F0, $94E3, $A604, $B211-$B30A). From the game part's use.

Address (with $8F) of the routine for_each_battle_party ($9F40) runs for each party on map $8D (JMP ($008E) at $9F6D): battle_round sets party_ranged_attacks $9F70, monsters_fire $9C65, melee_round $7F64 and resolve_orders $9EFD in turn ($B876-$B8A1). From the game part's use (its names).

High byte of the routine address at $8E ($B87C, $B88B, $B896, $B8A1). $90 after it: no reference in the parts' reachable code apart from the start-up's clearing of $02-$FF ($7F30-$7F37); the utility program's unreached printer code (send_report $8602) would clear $90-$AF for the KERNAL ($8645-$864C), with zero page saved before and put back after ($860E, $86A5).

Number of the map now at $3400, $FF for none: enter_map compares $09 with it and does nothing for the same map ($25BF), otherwise writes the old one back (save_map $2856, which skips $FF and every other number from $80 up, BMI at $2858) and records the new number ($25C8), a negative one as it is (load_map_pages translates it through T35/L8); load_map_pages, unpack_map_stream and the tile set check put it back in $09 ($262C, $271D, $25FC), save_dir_entry reads it ($285D) and the game compares the battle map with it ($B213). The game sets $FF at its start so the first map loads ($7E48); save_item_table borrows it ($26D9-$26E4). Module 4 sets $FF ($CBCA, $CC1A).

Number (0-127) of the portrait now unpacked in a picture buffer, $FF for none: load_portrait stores A AND $7F at $2639 after comparing at $2636 and unpacks entry $0505 ($265E); load_module ($26B8), unpack_map_stream ($26EF, when the buffer page $BA is $DE) and the game ($BF48, because the Order program is read into the $CA00 picture buffer) set $FF.

Prints message A of the engine's text block at the cursor, drawing each glyph at once: selects direct output ($1DB9: output vector $1DF9 = $1F03) and goes on at $0519; the vector stays direct afterwards. A is kept across the switch.
Prints message A of the engine's text block through whichever output routine is selected (JMP $0519). Reached from jump table $035F and from $0CEF and $11C1.
Sets the cursor to column X, row Y ($1EEC) and prints engine message A through the line buffer, as $0514. No JSR or JMP to $0511 was found in any part's snapshot.

Prints message A of the engine's text block through the line buffer: selects the buffered output ($1DC4: vector $1DF9 = $1F92, which collects a line at $F49C and breaks it at the window's right edge) and goes on at $0519. Used by the skill and item routines ($0CDA, $0E07, $0FC7, ...) and by $12A9.

Unpacks a packed stream (jump table $04F3; $2759 at $278D). Keeps A, X and Y, reads the unpacker's code from track 35, logical sector 16 into $C800 (over the third of the font's four pages, $C800-$C8FF: glyphs $60-$7F, the lower-case letters) through $053C, calls it at $C800 with A, X and Y as they came, then reads track 35, logical sector 11 back into $C800 (the font's own page) and returns through the disk read.
Reads one page from track Y, logical sector X into $C800-$C8FF: $FE/$FF = $C800, A = 1 page, through $284A (read pages, which retries through $27E8).

Not a variable: the operand ($FF) of the STA $FF at $0542. The animation code reaches the channel pointers $0549-$0550 as $0543+Y with Y = 6 + 2 x channel (LDA at $05FA, STA at $0627, $06D5 and $06DD), so the disassembler puts a table base here.

Here read_page_to_c800 sets A = 1 page and jumps to the page reader ($284A). The symbol on this instruction is the base $0544+Y that $0600 and $062D use, with Y = 6 + 2 x channel, for the high bytes of the channel pointers.

Script pointers of the picture's four animation channels, one word each (channel X at $0549 + 2X, low byte first): set from the picture header by $06D0 when a picture starts and when a channel's script ends ($0643), saved after each step by the tick at $05C5 ($0627/$062D), loaded into the stream reader's operand ($06C5/$06C6) before the next step.
Runs A ticks of the picture animation: calls $05C5 A times, counting down in $028B. Called by the text window's line feed ($210C, $2161), so the picture keeps moving while text scrolls.
Shows picture A from the buffer at $E000: sets bit 7 of A (the buffer flag that $2631 reads) and goes on at $055F. Jump table $041C.

Shows picture A (bit 7 set: buffer $E000, clear: $CA00): keeps it in $AB, loads it through $2631 unless it is already the picture in memory ($0505), turns the animation on ($AC = 1) and draws the picture window ($0568). Jump table $0419.

Draws the picture window: opens it ($12CF frames and clears the picture area, keeping the cursor and window variables, and sets $DF = 0, $B8 = 1), prints the picture's caption, the string at $F4D0 ("Ranger Ctr." in the play-map snapshot), under the picture at column 1, row 13 with direct output, keeping the cursor and window ($257E/$2563) and the string pointer $31/$32 ($2599 saves it in $25A4's operands, $25A4 puts it back), then starts the picture ($0586). Jump table $0416; the tick comes here ($05D8) when $B8 AND $DF is 0.

Starts the picture loaded at $B9/$BA: header bytes 0-3 go to $C1, $BF, $C2, $C0, the first column, first pixel row, last column and last pixel row of its area (1, $10, $0B, $63 in the snapshot; the frame decoder reads $BF, $C0 and $C2, and nothing was found reading $C1). The four animation channels point at their scripts (header words +6, +8, +10, +12, relative to the buffer; $06D0) with a countdown of 1 each in $DA-$DD, $DF and $B2 are set to 1, and the base picture (header word +4, relative) is drawn in store mode ($064E). Then it falls into one tick ($05C5). Jump table $041F.

One tick of the picture animation, from $0551, the key wait at $2534 and start_picture falling in. Nothing while $AC = 0. Unless $C5 is set, it first reloads the picture if a load replaced it ($2631 with $AB; carry set: restart at $0586) and redraws the window when $B8 AND $DF is 0 ($0568). A prescaler lets one call in 512 through ($B1 counts 256, $B2 2). Then each channel X = 0-3 whose enable byte $5BFB+X and header script word are not 0, and whose countdown $DA+X runs out, reads its next script entry: $FF restarts the script; otherwise a delay (to $DA+X) and a frame offset (relative to the buffer), and that frame is XORed onto the bitmap ($0648).
Operand of the LDX # at $063B: the tick's channel number (0-3). STX at $05E8 keeps it at the top of each pass because the frame decoder uses X; LDX, INX and CPX #4 then step to the next channel.
Draws the frame at the stream pointer ($06C5/$06C6) by XOR: patches $0692 to NOP (a $00 data byte then ends the block, and a new column, row and escape value follow) and $06AD to EOR abs, then $0651.
Draws the frame at the stream pointer ($06C5/$06C6) by storing: patches $0692 and $06AD to $2C (BIT abs), so a $00 data byte is stored like any other and the bitmap is not read; then $0651.

Decodes one frame into the bitmap at $6000, column by column: byte 0 is a pending run count (to $068A); then blocks of column X, pixel row Y and an escape value (to $0696; $FF as X ends the frame), each followed by data bytes written to successive pixel rows down the column (address from $2387 and $23A7), rows wrapping from $C0 back to $BF at the next column, until column $C2's row $C0 is written. A data byte equal to the escape value is followed by a count and a value: a run. In XOR mode a $00 data byte starts a new block.

Operand of the LDA # at $0689: bytes left in the current run. Set from the frame's first byte ($065A) and from the count after an escape byte ($069C), decremented at $06AA for each run byte written; while it is not 0 the BNE at $068B writes the run value instead of reading a data byte.

Opcode patched per frame: NOP ($EA) from draw_frame_xor, so the BEQ at $0693 takes a $00 data byte as the end of the block (back to $065D for a new column, row and escape value); BIT abs ($2C) from draw_frame_store, which swallows the BEQ so a $00 byte is drawn like any other.
Operand of the CMP # at $0695: the block's escape value, the third byte of its header ($066C). A data byte equal to it is not drawn; the next two bytes are a run count and a run value ($0699-$06A2).

Not a variable: the low byte ($C4) of the JSR $06C4 at $069F. The automatic symbol comes from the game's BIT $06A0 at $9EE0, which only hides a LDY #$06 (entered at $9EE1). Map 13 uses the same idiom: BIT $06A0 at $42E6 hides the LDY #$06 entered at $42E7 from $4283.

Operand of the LDA # at $06A8: the value of the current run, stored at $06A2 after the count. Nothing else sets it, so a frame whose first byte (the pending count) is not 0 starts with the value left from the last run decoded.

Opcode patched per frame: EOR abs ($4D) from draw_frame_xor, so the byte is XORed with the bitmap before the STA at $06B0 writes it back; BIT abs ($2C) from draw_frame_store, so the byte is stored as it is (the BIT only reads the bitmap).
Operand of the EOR (or BIT) at $06AD, low byte: the bitmap address of the current pixel row and column, copied from work_ptr at $0681 after $2387 and $23A7 have built it.
High byte of the EOR/BIT operand, stored at $0679 from add_column's result in A.
Operand of the STA at $06B0, low byte: the same bitmap address as $06AE, stored at $0684.
High byte of the STA operand at $06B0, stored at $067C.

Returns the next byte of the picture stream in A: LDA from the address in its own operand ($06C5/$06C6), then advances that address. N and Z come from the increment, not from the byte (callers compare it themselves); carry untouched.

Operand of the LDA at $06C4, low byte: the address of the next picture byte, incremented at $06C7. start_picture points it at the base frame ($05B7); the tick points it at a channel's script ($05FD), saves it back after the entry ($0624) and points it at the frame the entry names ($0635).
High byte of the stream address: set at $05BF, $0603 and $0631, carried into at $06CC, saved to the channel pointer from $062A.

Points an animation channel at the start of its script: the header word at ($B9)+Y plus the buffer base $B9/$BA, stored at $0543+Y and $0544+Y (Y = 6 + 2 x channel, so $0549 + 2 x channel). Returns with Y one higher. Called by $0586 for each channel and by the tick when a script ends ($0643).

Divides A (low) and X (high) by Y: clears the dividend's top byte $073F and goes on at $06E8. Jump table $0410; the game calls it at $86E3 and $8723, and map 20's minutes_to_hours jumps to it at $40FF.

Returns the quotient in $073D-$073F (A = low, X = middle) and the remainder in $D3. A divisor of 0 gives a quotient of all ones. Entered here by $0E38 with the viewed member's 24-bit cash (loaded into $1C-$1E by cash_load and passed as A, X and $073F) and Y = $07, the number of party members.
Low byte of the division's 24-bit dividend and quotient: $06E8 stores A here, each round shifts it left (ASL at $06FD) and sets bit 0 when the divisor went in ($0730); returned in A ($0736).
Middle byte of the dividend and quotient: X at $06EB, rotated at $0700, returned in X ($0739).
Top byte of the dividend and quotient: 0 from $06E1, or the caller's before $06E8 (view_divide_cash at $0E2F); rotated at $0703, read back by $0E3F.
The divisor, from Y at $06EE; compared at $0717 and subtracted at $071F. 0 gives a quotient of $FFFFFF.

Plays the third sound of the SID routine's table: X = $16 (offset 22 into the 11-byte records at $C9BC), then $C993. Shakes the screen: plays sound 0 ($C993 with X = 0), saves $D011 and $D016, then 12 times waits ($242B with A = $80) and gives both registers a random fine scroll in bits 0-2 ($077A); restores $D016 and $D011 as saved and turns voice 1's gate off ($D404 = 0). Both registers keep their other bits as read, $D011's bit 7 included (the raster's high bit when read, the raster compare's when written). Returns with the carry random_byte ($24E3) left from its ADC of the seed rnd_seed (the operand at $24ED, which every call rewrites) at $24EC in the last jolt: nothing after the last JSR $077A ($0764) touches it. Map code that ends JMP $044C (maps 3, 4, 9, 12, 18, 20, 27, 31, 33, 35, 36 and 39) hands that carry to run_action (game $8872), which redraws the view only when it is set, so the redraw after a blast is chance.
Operand of the LDX # at $0767: jolts left in the screen shake, 12 from $0753, stored at $0755 each pass because X carries the register offset for $077A; LDX, DEX and BNE at $0767-$076A count it down.

Gives the VIC register $D011+X (X = 0: $D011, X = 5: $D016) a random fine scroll: keeps its bits 3-7 as read, takes bits 0-2 from a random number ($24E3); the ORA operand at $0788 holds the kept bits.
Operand of the ORA # at $0787: $077F stores here the register's bits 3-7 as read, so the ORA puts them back over the random bits 0-2.
Clears the 16-bit number $6F/$70 (check_total): A = X = 0, then the store at $0790; returns A = X = 0 with Z set. Jump table $03E0; called directly by $0C6D, $0D18, $0D77 and $150A.
Sets $6F/$70 = A (low), X (high). Jump table $0401; num1_add_clamped stores its limit through it ($07BE).
Clears the 16-bit number $71/$72 (check_target): A = X = 0, then the store at $0798; returns A = X = 0 with Z set. Jump table $03E6; called directly by $0C2F, $0D1B, $0D6E and $1507.
Sets $71/$72 = A (low), X (high). Jump table $0404; num2_add_clamped stores its limit through it ($07E7).

Adds the signed 16-bit number X:A (negative when X bit 7 is set) to $6F/$70 and holds the result within 0-$FFFF: a positive addend that carries out gives $FFFF, a negative one that borrows gives 0. Returns A/X = $6F/$70; the carry is as the add left it. Jump table $03E3; called directly by $0C7C, $0C8F, $0C9B, $0D3C, $0D45, $0D7E, $0D8A, $1527, $1530 and $1536.

Plain 16-bit add of X:A to $6F/$70 (CLC first) for num1_add_clamped, whose test is the carry out: set on overflow for a positive addend, clear on a drop below 0 for a negative one. Returns A = the new high byte.

Adds the signed 16-bit number X:A to $71/$72 the same way: a positive addend that carries out gives $FFFF, a negative one that borrows gives 0. Returns A/X = $71/$72. Jump table $03E9; called directly by $0C37, $0D23, $0D74 and $151D.
Plain 16-bit add of X:A to $71/$72 (CLC first) for num2_add_clamped; returns A = the new high byte and the carry out.
Returns A (low), X (high) = $6F/$70 - $71/$72 without storing it; carry clear when $71/$72 is the larger (the difference went below 0); N and Z come from the low byte (PLA). Jump table $03EC.

Compares $6F/$70 with $71/$72 as unsigned 16-bit numbers: carry set when $6F/$70 is at least $71/$72. Then (JMP $0811 at $0805, into the equality test that $0808, jump table $03F5, also ends in) A = 0 with Z set when the two are equal, else A = $FF with Z clear; PHP/PLP keep the carry. Jump table $03F2; called directly by $0C4C, $0D48, $0D8D and $1539.

Second half of the word comparison that starts at $07FC (LDA $6F / CMP $71, the low bytes): subtracts the high bytes, $70 - $72, so that carry is set when $6F/$70 >= $71/$72, pushes the flags and jumps to the equality test compare_word_equal ($0811).

Entry $03F5; the game calls it at $829C. Compares the 16-bit words $71/$72 and $6F/$70 (low byte first): carry set when $71/$72 >= $6F/$70 (unsigned), clear when below; A = 0 with Z set when they are equal, A = $FF otherwise. X and Y kept. The equality test is the tail at $0811, shared with $07FC, which compares the other way round (carry set when $6F/$70 >= $71/$72).

Shared tail of the word comparisons $07FC (by JMP from $0805) and $0808 (falling through), entered with the comparison's flags pushed: A = 0 (Z set) when $6F/$70 equals $71/$72, A = $FF (Z clear) when not; the carry pulled back by PLP is the comparison's.

Entry $03DD. Adds the 24-bit number in $1C-$1E (low byte first) to the current character's experience, record bytes +$21..+$23 at ($66). A sum past $FFFFFF is held at $FFFFFF ($1389 stores A = $FF at +$21..+$23). Callers: skill_check ($0C49) and attribute_check ($0D35) with the dice roll, the game ($8163, $8166, $90F2, $A08A, $A719). Returns Y = $23.

Entry $03F8. Open-ended 2d6: rolls two dice (roll_d6, $24D6, so the random seed moves) and adds both to a running total; while the two dice show the same number it rolls another pair and adds that too. Returns A = the total, X = 0; Y kept. The total is eight bits and is not checked for wrapping. Callers: skill_roll_total ($0C70), attribute_check ($0D26), npc_obey_check ($0D81), $1520, the game ($7FD2, $802F, $9CF3, $A46B, $A58D, $A899).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $0855, written at $084D: the first die of the pair just rolled by roll_2d6_open; CPX $0856 at $085C compares the second die with it to spot a double.
Operand of the ADC #imm at $0857: roll_2d6_open's running total, cleared at $0847, rewritten after every pair at $0859 and returned from $0861.
a double: roll another pair

Entry $03FB. Returns 15 + 5*X as a 16-bit number: A = low byte, X and Y = high byte (X = 0 gives 15, X = 255 gives 1290). The target a check must reach at difficulty X: skill_check ($0C34), attribute_check ($0D20), npc_obey_check ($0D71), $151A, the game ($8D51).

Entry $03FE. Multiplies A by 4 into 16 bits: A = the low byte, X = the high byte (A's top two bits). Y kept. Used for 4 x a skill level: skill_roll_total ($0C98), weapon_skill_bonus ($0DCD, by JMP), the game ($8247).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $088B: times_four stores A here ($087D) and shifts it left twice in place ($0882, $0886), so the LDA returns the low byte of A*4.

Entry $0407. Subtracts the 16-bit amount A (low) / X (high) from the current character's CON, record bytes +$1D/+$1E at ($66): no floor, so CON can go to 0 or below (negative values read as bit 7 of +$1E). Returns A = the new high byte, Y = $1E, carry clear when the subtraction borrowed. Callers: con_heal_one, the game ($A925, $B85D, $B864).
Operand of the SBC #imm at $0899, written at $088E: the low byte of the amount con_subtract takes from CON (+$1D).
Operand of the SBC #imm at $08A0, written at $0891: the high byte of the amount con_subtract takes from CON (+$1E).

Entry $040A. Heals the current character by one point: con_subtract with $FFFF adds 1 to CON (+$1D/+$1E), then con_is_full ($1493) compares CON with MAXCON (+$1B/+$1C): carry clear when they are now equal, carry set otherwise. It does not check first, so a character already at MAXCON goes above it and gets carry set. Module 0 calls it after each payment ($CB34), and again at $CB3D when CON is then exactly 0.

Not a variable: the low byte of the JSR con_subtract operand at $08A8. The automatic symbol comes from the BIT $08A9 at $239A (and the ranger program's $7F3E), a BIT that only hides the LDA #$08 at $239B; the byte it reads is thrown away.

Entry $040D. Counts the conscious members of the current party ($08): for each position from $07 (the party size) down to 1, member_is_conscious ($17E6) selects that member (select_member, so $66/$67 and $BB change) and tests CON >= 1. Returns A = the count, and leaves member 1 as the current character. A party size of 0 is not caught: the count would run through positions 0 and 255 down to 1. Called by the game ten times ($7F0C, $81B7, $960E, ...).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $08C6: the party position count_conscious is testing, from $07 down to 1 (written at $08BB, counted down at $08C9).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $08CD: count_conscious's tally of conscious members, cleared at $08B6 and raised at $08C3; the LDA returns it.

Entry $0413. Carry clear when item class A is in ranged_classes ($08E8: every class from 2 to 13), carry set when it is not (classes 0, 1, 14, 15 and 16 up). A is kept; Y = where the search stopped. The roster's AMM column ($16A1) prints the weapon's rounds only for these classes; the game calls it twelve times ($7FB1, $8443, $9CA9, ...).
Operand of the CMP #imm at $08DB, written at $08D0: the item class class_is_ranged looks for in ranged_classes.

Item classes counted as ranged weapons by class_is_ranged ($08D6), ended by $FF: 13, 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, that is every class from 2 to 13. In the item table at $3108 those are pistols and thrown weapons (2), the flamethrower, rifles, SMGs and assault rifles (3-7; no item has class 5), rockets (8-9), energy weapons (10-12) and explosives (13); not in the list are 1 (fists and melee weapons), 14 (clips, shells, power packs), 15 (armour) and 16 up (other items, cash).

Entry $04CF. Distance from the party's square ($57/$58) to map square X, Y in tenths of a square: |dy| ($0907) and |dx| ($090D) through abs_value ($23FE), then entry 10*|dy| + |dx| of distance_table ($0921). Returns A = the distance, Y = the index, X kept. Valid only for |dx| <= 9 and |dy| <= 4, the 19 x 9 view; nothing checks it, and a larger offset reads the wrong row or the code after the table. Callers: draw_square ($0B77, the Geiger reading), the game nine times ($7F8E, $8521, $95C1, ...), mostly on the x, y of records at ($79).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $0906, written at $08FF: |dy|, the rows between the square and the party. Added twice to 8*|dy| (the ADC itself, then ADC $0907 at $0908) to make 10*|dy|.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $090C: first the square's column X (written at $08F5), then |dx|, the columns between it and the party (written at $0914 and added at $0919).

Fifty distances in tenths of a square, five rows of ten: entry 10*dy + dx (dy 0-4, dx 0-9) is about 10 x sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy), rounded or cut: 2 (not 0) for the party's own square, 10 20 ... 90 along a row, 14 for one diagonal step, 98 for the far corner (dx 9, dy 4). Read by distance_to_party ($091D).

Entry $0425. Returns A = the class (0-15) of map square X, Y from the class layer at $3400 (4 bits a square, two squares a byte): row Y is width/2 bytes from $3400 + Y*width/2 (width $56; the multiply works for a power of two, 32 or 64 in practice), byte X/2 of it, the high nibble for an even X ($0989), the low one for an odd X. The row's address stays in $5B/$5C and $63 holds its number, so a call on the same row skips the multiply (enter_map sets $63 = $FF). X kept, Y = X/2; $12/$13 used.
width odd: row base not recomputed
+ $3400, the class layer's base (low byte here, high byte at $097A)
high byte of the class layer's base $3400
Operand of the LDA #imm at $097E, written at $0953: the column X whose class map_class_at returns; halved to index the row, its low bit picks the nibble.
Shifts A right four times, leaving its high nibble in the low four bits: map_class_at's even-column exit, also called on its own by print_bcd_pair ($1CCB) for a BCD digit.
Shifts A right three times (A / 8). Entered by item_class ($144E, by JMP) to turn byte 3 of an item record into the item's class.

Entry $0422. Points $5D/$5E at row Y of the map's number layer (one byte a square), which follows the class layer: $3400 + height*width/2 + Y*width (height $55, width $56). map_class_at with X = width, Y = height finds the layer's start, so $5B/$5C, $63 and $12/$13 change too. Returns X = width, Y = width/2. Callers: map_number_at, set_square ($0A4C), the game ($9553).

Entry $0428. Points $5F/$60 at the action record for class Y (0-15) and number A: the map record at $61/$62 holds at +6 + 2*Y the address of class Y's table (one word per number), and word A of that table is the record's address. $12/$13 is left on the class's table. A number of 128 or more wraps (2*A is eight bits), and a class whose table word is 0 reads from $0000. Callers: square_record ($0BC5), the game ($885E, $A426, $B028, $B133, $BB8B) and the code of maps 4 ($41B5, $41E6), 8 ($3EE2), 13 ($433E, $434E), 21 ($3C9F, $3CAF), 32 ($3ED1, $3EE1, $3F2A), 33 ($3E1C, $3E2C), 38 ($3FC4), 40 ($3E86), 41 ($4230, $4240, $4280), 43 ($3E61, $3E71) and 49 ($3E3B).

Entry $042B. Reads both layers of map square X, Y: returns A = its class (map_class_at), X = its number from the number layer (map_number_at), Y = the column. Changes $5B/$5C, $5D/$5E, $63 and $12/$13. Callers: alter_square ($0A1B), the game ($8780, $B12D, $B13B, $BB7E, $BDEC; at $ACDB-$ACF0 the class of the party's square picks the game's handler from its table at $ACF3) and map 25's code ($3FB4, $3FC3, $3FD2).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $09EB, written at $09E1: the column map_square_at was asked for, kept across map_class_at.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $09ED, written at $09E4: the row map_square_at was asked for, kept across map_class_at.

Entry $0443. Returns the number of map square X, Y, from the number layer, in A and X (map_number_row for row Y, then byte X of it); Y = the column. Changes $5B/$5C, $5D/$5E, $63, $12/$13. Called by map_square_at and square_record; no other part calls the entry.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $09FA, written at $09F4: the column map_number_at reads from the number layer's row ($5D).

Entry $042E. Changes map square X, Y as the action record at ($5F) says: offset A of the record holds the new class and number. The square's present class and number are first copied to $AD/$AE. A class byte of $FE puts back the square saved there by the last change (the two trade places, $0A28); $FD does the same and always returns carry clear; any other byte with bit 7 set writes nothing, though the square is still copied to $AD/$AE. Carry set when the square was written. Callers: the game ($88B7, $8CAD, $8CFF, $8F6C, $918F, $B109, $BB72).
$FE: swap with the saved square
$FD: swap, then carry clear

Class byte $FE (and $FD through $0A38): takes the square saved in $AD/$AE as the new class and byte ($64/$65) and goes on at $0A18, which saves the square being replaced in $AD/$AE first, so the two trade places.
Returns X/Y = the square alter_square was called with, kept in the operands of these LDX/LDY (written at $0A00/$0A03).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $0A33, written at $0A03: the column of the square alter_square changes.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $0A35, written at $0A00: the row of the square alter_square changes.

Entry $0434. Writes map square X, Y: the class in $64 into the class layer (set_class_at) and the number in $65 into the number layer (map_number_row), and returns carry set; when $64 has bit 7 set nothing is written and carry is clear. Also the end of alter_square. Callers: the game ($878F and $87AD, where a square's contents move to the next square; $B0C8), module 4 ($CBDF).
class byte with bit 7 set: write nothing
Operand of the LDY #imm at $0A4A, written at $0A44: the row set_square writes, for map_number_row.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $0A4F, written at $0A41: the column set_square writes in the number layer row ($5D).

Entry $0431 (no other part calls it; set_square does, at $0A47). Writes class A into the class layer at map square X, Y, keeping the other square's nibble of the byte: shifted into the high nibble for an even X, ORed in as it is for an odd X. A is not masked, so a value of 16 or more would change the even neighbour's class too.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $0A60, written at $0A5A: the column set_class_at writes; halved to index the row, its low bit picks the nibble.
Operand of the ORA #imm at $0A7A, written at $0A57: the class set_class_at writes, moved into the high nibble for an even column ($0A6D-$0A73).

Entry $0437. Sets the party's square $57/$58 from the view: X = $02 + $59, Y = $03 + $5A (the view's top-left square plus 9 and 4, through view_center), and returns it in X/Y. Callers: the game ($AC72, $AC95, $AE07, $AF1D).

Entry $043A. Returns X = $02 + $59 and Y = $03 + $5A: the square in the middle of the 19 x 9 view, which is the party's, without storing it. Falls into add_view_offset. Callers: party_square, the game ($ACC1, $ACDB, $ACED, $B138, $BDE9).

Entry $043D. Adds the view offsets to the square in X/Y: X + $59, Y + $5A (9 and 4 from enter_map), the step from the view's top-left square to the one the party stands on. The game calls it at $AD98.

Entry $0440. Subtracts the view offsets from the square in X/Y: X - $59, Y - $5A, the step from the party's square to the view's top-left square. The game uses it before storing $02/$03 when the party is put on a square ($89F4: the party's previous return point, party table +$0B/+$0C, for an exit to map $FF; $8A1B: the exit record's x and y, added to the party's square when the record's byte 0 has bit 7 set).

Entry $04E1. Draws the Geiger counter's gauge at columns 38-39 (the window's right edge $26 set to 39), from row 17 up to row 0, two glyphs a row through print_char_direct ($1F03). The lowest 18 - $9F/8 rows are drawn with glyphs $80/$82 in colour byte $62, the rows above with glyphs $7E/$5B in the colour $EB (kept). $9F is the distance, in tenths of a square, to the nearest class-9 square drawn in the view (draw_square, $0B7A), $FF when nobody carries a Geiger counter (game $B176-$B192): $9F/8 of 18 or more draws none. The cursor and window $23-$28 are kept (push_zp23, then JMP $255F). Callers: the game ($ACBE), the start-up ($814B: $FF at $7F8C and $800E, then $40 down to 1 as the title's bombs fall), the utilities ($7E1C) and module 4 ($CB24), both with $9F = $FF.
$9F = 0 leaves the count at 0: 256 steps
$9F/8 of 18 or more: no coloured steps

Operand of the SBC #imm at $0AC6 and draw_geiger_gauge's counter: 0 ($0AB2), then $9F/8 ($0AC0) so that the SBC gives 18 - $9F/8, then the number of coloured steps still to draw ($0AC8, counted down at $0AE2).
until the row passes 0

Entry $0449 (no other part calls it; draw_square does, at $0BA0). Points $7B/$7C at row Y of the map's tile layer at $DE00, one tile number a square: $DE00 + Y*width ($56). The layer is RAM under the I/O area, so a reader banks all RAM in first ($25AD). $12/$13 used.
+ $DE00, the tile layer's base (low byte here, high byte at $0B21)
high byte of the tile layer's base $DE00
Shifts A left four times (A * 16, low byte): the class into the high nibble in set_class_at ($0A70), rows to pixel lines in square_to_screen ($0B38).

Entry $04D8. Screen position of map square X, Y for draw_tile: X = column 2*(X - $02), Y = pixel line 16*(Y - $03), both eight bits, from the view's top-left square $02/$03. With the roster hidden ($6A = 0) it always returns carry clear and leaves the clipping to draw_tile (columns 1-36, lines 8-135); with the roster shown carry is set for a pixel line of 14 or more, so only the view's top row passes. Callers: draw_square ($0BB2), the game ($9605, $AD3C, $AF20).
roster shown: only pixel lines 0-13 count as on screen

Entry $04D5. Carry clear when square X, Y lies on the map: X below the width $56 and Y below the height $55 (unsigned, so a negative coordinate is off the map too); carry set when outside. Callers: draw_square ($0B59), the game ($8662, $ADB0).

Entry $04DB. Draws map square X, Y of the view. The tile: off the map, byte +$33 of the map record ($61); class 5, tile 5; class 4, byte 1 of its action record (square_record) AND $7F; class 9, its distance to the party (distance_to_party) lowers $9F, the Geiger reading, and from 18:00 to 5:59 (hour $0E) it is tile 8, the radiation sign, the same bytes in all nine tile sets; otherwise the tile layer's number ($0B06, read with all RAM banked in). Then square_to_screen and draw_tile ($22D8), or carry set when off the screen. Changes $5F/$60 for class 4. Callers: the game's view drawing ($AEBA a column, $AEDF a row, $AFBB the special squares, $AF2F, $9837).
map record +$33: the tile drawn off the map
class 5: tile 5
class 4: tile from the action record
class 9 (radiation): Geiger distance, night tile
hour below 6: night
hour 6-17: day, the tile layer's tile
night: tile 8, the radiation sign

For a class-4 square in draw_square: points $5F/$60 at its action record: class A (pushed), number from the number layer at the square kept in draw_square_xy ($09F4), then action_record with Y = the class.
Returns X/Y = the square draw_square was called with, kept in the operands of these LDX/LDY (written at $0B53/$0B56).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $0BC8, written at $0B53: the column draw_square is drawing; also read at $0BA6 to index the tile layer row.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $0BCA, written at $0B56: the row draw_square is drawing.

Entry $03C8. Points $16/$17 at item A's eight-byte record in the item table, $3108 + 8*A, through record_address ($1AFE): sets $45/$46 = $3108 and $4C = 8, which stay set for later calls of record_address ($039E), their only reader: module 1's buy code calls it at $CBF2 for the item picked from its list, relying on item_record's setting ($CC62). Returns A = $16, Y = $17, X = 0. Item numbers are 0-94 (to $33FF); nothing checks A. Callers: the engine ($0DD0, $10BC, $122B, $1270, $1451), the game, module 1 and the Ranger Center.

Entry $03CB. Prints the name of item A: engine message A + 36 ($24) through print_engine_msg ($0519), so $43/$44 is left on the engine's text block ($29E4).
