The current output (direct or word-wrapped) is used, and the count $38 picks the singular or plural ending ({0A}). Callers: $11ED, print_weapon_name ($1715), the game ($9367), module 1, the utilities.

Entry $03D1. Carry clear when the class of the item whose record is at ($16) (item_class, $144A: byte 3 / 8) is in the list at ($9D), which ends with $FF; Y = its place in the list. Carry set when it is not there. Callers: count_items_of_classes ($122E), module 1 ($CB73, $CC70, $CCA4).
Operand of the CMP #imm at $0BF0, written at $0BE5: the class of the item at ($16), which item_class_in_list looks for in the list at ($9D).

Entry $03CE. Pays the 24-bit amount in $1C-$1E (low byte first) from the current character's cash, record bytes +$15..+$17 at ($66): cash_compare ($0C18) first, and only when the cash covers it does the subtraction at $0C00 run. Carry set = paid, carry clear = too little cash and nothing taken. Callers: the game ($90D2), module 0 ($CB2F before healing a point, $CBA1 before clearing a condition bit of +$28, $CBD9), module 1 ($CC0C).

Second half of spend_cash ($0BFB, entry $03CE), reached when cash_compare found the cash sufficient: subtracts the 24-bit amount in $1C-$1E from the current character's cash at ($66)+$15..+$17. Leaves Y = $17.

Entry $03D4. Compares the current character's 24-bit cash at ($66)+$15..+$17 with the amount in $1C-$1E: carry set when cash >= amount (can pay), clear when short. Changes A and Y ($17); writes nothing. Callers: spend_cash $0BFB, the game ($8E7E), module 1.

Entry $0207. Skill check for the current character ($66): A = skill (1-35), X = difficulty. Target ($71/$72) = 15 + 5*X ($0867). skill_roll_total gives roll + governing attribute + 4*level in $6F/$70; a roll under 5 fails at once. Otherwise the roll is added to experience (+$21..+$23, $0825), and if the total reaches the target the check succeeds (carry clear) and skill_improve_roll may raise the skill. Carry set = failure. Called by the game ($8EB4, $8FE6).
Operand of LDX #imm at $0C32, written at entry (STX $0C33): the difficulty X of skill_check, read back at $0C54 for skill_improve_roll.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0C3A, written at entry (STA $0C3B): the skill number A of skill_check, read back at $0C51 for skill_improve_roll.
A = skill number: points $16/$17 at skill_attribute_table + A ($0DD8 + A, with carry into the high byte). Returns A = $17.

Entry $020A. Roll for skill A of the current character: $6F/$70 cleared, $0845 rolls 2d6 (rolling again on doubles); a roll under 5 returns carry set (automatic failure). Otherwise $6F/$70 = roll + the attribute named by skill_attribute_table (none for entry 0) + 4 * the level from skill_level, clamped at $FFFF by $079D; returns A = the roll, carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0C7F, written at entry (STA $0C80): the skill number of skill_roll_total, read back at $0C92 for skill_level.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0C9E, written at $0C77: the 2d6 roll, returned in A by skill_roll_total.

Entry $020F. Learning by use: A = skill, X = difficulty of the check just passed. Nothing happens unless the current character has the skill (level >= 1), the level is below his rank (+$24) and below X. Then a d10 ($24C4) at or under (X - level)/2 + 1 raises the level by one (it stops at 255), and the text window says "<name> raised his/her <skill> skill to level n." (messages 158, the skill name, 159), with a (RETURN) prompt when the window had to be opened.

Not a variable: this is the low byte of the JSR skill_level operand at $0CA8. The only reference is the game's BIT $0CA9 at $8DBB, the two-byte skip trick that hides an LDA #$0C, which the tracer took for an access.
Operand of CMP #imm at $0CB6, written at entry (STX $0CB7): the difficulty X of skill_improve_roll; the level must be below it, and LDA $0CB7 at $0CBA reads it for the chance.
Operand of SBC #imm at $0CBE, written at $0CB3: the skill's current level, subtracted from the difficulty to give the chance.
Operand of CMP #imm at $0CCC, written at $0CC4: the improvement chance (difficulty - level)/2 + 1; a d10 at or under it raises the skill.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0CDD, written at entry (STA $0CDE): the skill number of skill_improve_roll, used to find and print the skill once it improves.

Entry $0212. Attribute check for the current character: Y = record offset, A = difficulty. Y = $18 (sex) passes when the byte equals A; Y = $24 (rank) passes when rank >= A. Any other offset: target 15 + 5*A ($0867) against 2d6 (doubles roll again; under 5 fails) + the byte at Y, and the roll is added to experience ($0825). Carry clear = pass. Called by the game ($8E98, $901D).
Operand of LDX #imm at $0D1E, written at entry (STA $0D1F): the difficulty A of attribute_check; CMP $0D1F at $0D51 and $0D5A compares the rank or sex byte with it directly.
Operand of LDY #imm at $0D3F, written at entry (STY $0D40): the record offset of the attribute being tested.

Entry $021F. Willingness check for the current character, an NPC: Y = offset of one of its refusal bytes (the trade code uses +$2E; the game's $8D83-$8D95 uses +$2B-+$2D with A = +$31), A = the value it is tested against (for a trade, the taker's CHR). A byte of $FF always refuses. Otherwise target 15 + 5*byte against A + 2d6: a roll under 5 refuses and raises the byte (char_byte_increment); a pass lowers it with a 1 in 20 chance (char_byte_decrement). Carry clear = willing.

Operand of LDA #imm at $0D7A, written at entry (STA $0D7B): the value A that npc_obey_check adds to its roll. In a trade it is the taker's CHR (+$14, $0F70-$0F7E); in the game's Use refusals ($8D8E-$8D95) it is the NPC's own byte +$31, which hiring set to the hirer's CHR ($A403, $A492).
Operand of LDY #imm at $0D9B, written at entry (STY $0D9C): the offset of the NPC's refusal byte, used to lower it (pass) or, through LDY $0D9C at $0DA2, to raise it (roll under 5).
Entry $021A. Decrements the current character's byte at ($66)+Y unless it is already 0. Called by npc_obey_check and the game ($A4A6-$A4AE).
Entry $0217. Increments the current character's byte at ($66)+Y unless it is exactly 10: a byte already above 10 keeps rising. Called by npc_obey_check and the game ($A4E2-$A4EA).

Entry $0227. A/X = 4 * the current character's level in the skill of the equipped weapon (item record byte 5, via item_skill_number and skill_level); with nothing equipped it uses Fists, item 0, whose skill is Pugilism. Leaves $16/$17 at that item's record. Used by unjam_weapon and the game ($8126, $A5D0).
Entry $0222. A = item number: points $16/$17 at its eight-byte record ($0BCD: $3108 + 8*A) and returns A = record byte 5, the number of the skill that governs the item (0 for none), with Y = 5.

skill_attribute_table: 36 bytes, one per skill number 0-35 (read through skill_attr_ptr): the record offset of the attribute added to a skill roll. $0E ST, $0F IQ, $10 LK, $11 SP, $12 AGL, $13 DEX, $14 CHR; entry 0 is $00 (none). Brawling and Gamble LK; Climb, Acrobat and Silent move AGL; Pugilism and Swim ST; Combat shooting (17) SP; Confidence and Bureaucracy CHR; DEX for the weapon skills (Clip pistol, Knife fight, Rifle, Knife throw, Assault rifle, AT weapon, SMG, Energy weapon) and for Picklock, Sleight of hand, Forgery, Safecrack and Helicopter pilot; IQ for Perception and the technical skills (Demolitions, Alarm disarm, Bomb disarm, Medic, Cryptology, Metallurgy, Electronics, Toaster repair, Doctor, Clone tech, Cyborg tech).

Entries $0332 and $033B. Character screen for party member A (the game's view of one character, $AC6C; the Ranger Center, $7F48). Highlights the roster line, prints the sheet (print_character_sheet) and "P)ool D)iv cash" (message 140), then waits: P pools all the party's cash to this member, D divides it, RETURN or space goes on to the items page (view_items_loop) and from there to the skills page (skills_page). Left-arrow goes back one page: from the sheet it leaves. On the skills page, RETURN, space or a skill number leaves, and so does a character with no skills; with no items the items page is skipped. On leaving, the roster line is redrawn plain.

Operand of LDA #imm at $0E1F, written at entry (STA $0E20): the member number shown by view_character. The pool code uses it as the receiver; LDA $0E20 reads it back throughout the item, trade and divide code ($0E24-$0FBC).

The D key of the character screen: divides this member's cash among the $07 members of the party. $06E8 divides the 24-bit cash by $07; the member's cash is cleared, each member (this one included) gets the quotient (cash_add), and this member also gets the remainder from $D3-$D5. Then the screen is redrawn.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0E52, written at $0E49: the member counter (1 to $07) of the divide loop.

Item menu for slot A of the current character, called from view_items_loop. When the slot holds the ammunition of the equipped weapon (weapon record byte 7) it asks "Reload (Y/N)?" and Y reloads (reload_weapon). When the item's count byte has bit 7 set (jammed) it asks "Unjam (Y/N)?", the Y drawn as glyph $7C (a reverse-video Y), and any key but N or left-arrow tries unjam_weapon. Otherwise, and after N or left-arrow at either question, it offers D)rop, T)rade and unE)quip (equip_toggle).
Operand of LDA #imm at $0EAC, written at entry (STA $0EAD): the item slot of item_action_menu, read back by the drop ($0F04), equip ($0F13) and trade ($0F51) code.
Operand of LDY #imm at $0ECB, written at $0EB1: the record offset of the slot's item byte (+$BB + 2*slot), read back by LDY $0ECC at $0ED0 and $0EE2.
D)rop, and the last step of a trade: clears the slot held at $0EAD (item and count bytes, clear_pair), then unequip_slot forgets it if it was the weapon or the armour.

T)rade: with one member, "No one to trade with."; with two, the other member takes it (member number EOR 3); otherwise "Who wants it?" and pick_member (not the giver). An NPC giver (+$29 non-zero) that is conscious must pass npc_obey_check (its +$2E against the taker's CHR) or "doesn't want to trade". A taker with 30 items "can't carry any more". The item and its count byte go to the taker's first free slot and are dropped from the giver.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0F99, written at $0F5A: the item number being traded, stored in the taker's free slot.
Operand of LDA #imm at $0F9E, written at $0F60: the traded item's count byte (rounds or charges, jam flag), stored in the taker's slot.

Items page of the character screen: item_list_page for the member at $0E20; each item chosen goes to item_action_menu and the member's roster line is redrawn. RETURN, space or left-arrow ends it, and so does a member with no items, returned in A (0 no items, $FD RETURN or space, $FF left-arrow) with carry set. R reorders the list inside item_list_page and the list comes back; when the items fill more than one page the paging keys of list_choose turn it ($19C2-$19E0); other keys are ignored (list_choose $19A4-$19B3).

Entry $04E4 (also used by the Ranger Center, $80AA). Prints the current character's sheet in the text window: message 137 ("NAME: " and the name; its code 7 opens the window), print_attributes, "SEX: " with Male or Female (messages 162 + byte +$18) and "NATIONALITY: " with U.S., Russian, Mexican, Indian or Chinese (messages 145 + byte +$19).

Entry $0347. Item list of party member A (select_member): returns the chosen slot with carry clear, or with carry set A = 0 (no items), $FD (RETURN/space) or $FF (left-arrow). R starts a reorder: the player picks every item in the new order (each moved to $5A00 by move_pair_to_buffer) until none is left, then the list is copied back to +$BD..+$F8, the weapon and armour slot numbers (+$1F, +$25) are replaced from $1026 and $102C, and the list is shown again.

R on the item list: clears the 60-byte buffer at $5A00, then lists " Reorder" repeatedly; each item picked moves to the next buffer pair, and the slot number it will get ($103F) is noted when it is the weapon or the armour. Left-arrow, RETURN, space and R also advance $103F without moving an item (see $1015); other keys stay inside list_choose (ignored, or turning the page).

Operand of LDA #imm at $1025: the new slot number of the equipped weapon, written at $1046 when the weapon is picked during a reorder and stored into +$1F. Never reset: a character with no weapon equipped gets the value left by an earlier reorder.
Operand of LDA #imm at $102B: the new slot number of the equipped armour, written at $104F during a reorder and stored into +$25. Never reset, like $1026.

Operand of LDX #imm at $103E: the slot number the next picked item will have (1, 2, ...), cleared at $0FF9 and raised at $1015 before each list, including after left-arrow, RETURN, space or R, which move nothing.
Operand of LDX #imm at $1056: the index in the $5A00 buffer where the next picked item pair goes, cleared at $0FF6 and advanced by move_pair_to_buffer.

Item list: counts the current character's items (count_items); none returns A = 0, carry set. Otherwise opens the text window with "Item" (message 151) and title message A (0 none, 168 " Reorder"), draws the first page, at most nine lines, of the items in slots 1-30 through print_item_row (vector $47/$48, list code $19ED, $4D = 31) with R as the extra key ($BE = $D2), and waits ($1975). Returns carry clear with A = the chosen slot ($49), or carry set with A = $FD (RETURN/space), $FE (R) or $FF (left-arrow).
Operand of LDA #imm at $1076, written at entry (STA $1077): the title message printed under "Item" (0 for none, 168 for " Reorder").

Entry $0389. unE)quip for slot A of the current character, a toggle: a slot already equipped as weapon (+$1F) or armour (+$25) is unequipped (unequip_slot). Otherwise an item of class 15 (armour, item_class) becomes the armour (+$25) and sets AC (+$1A) to its record byte 6; any other item, even a canteen or a clip, becomes the weapon (+$1F).
Operand of LDA #imm at $10B4, written at entry (STA $10B5): the slot being equipped, stored by LDA $10B5 at $10D2 into +$1F or +$25.

Entry $0362. A = slot: if it is the current character's weapon (+$1F) that field becomes 0; if it is the armour (+$25) that field and the AC (+$1A) become 0. Called after an item leaves a slot (drop, trade, last charge used), by equip_toggle ($10B1) to unequip, and by module 1 ($CB0C).

Entry $032F (also the Ranger Center, $801F). Prints the attribute block of the current character in the window, three-digit fields: ST IQ LK on one line, SP AGL DEX, then CHR and SKP (+$0E..+$14, +$20), "RANK:" and the rank name from +$32, "MAXCON=" (+$1B/+$1C) and "$=" with the 24-bit cash (+$15..+$17). The labels are the strings at attribute_labels, printed in turn by $1DD8. Its first instruction, JSR flush_line ($1FFB), overwrites A, so a value passed in A is ignored.
Prints the current character's byte at ($66)+Y as a decimal number in a field of width $30 ($1C83).

attribute_labels: the zero-terminated strings print_attributes prints in turn, in the font's ASCII order ($0D new line, $03 clear to the end of the line): "ST =", " IQ =", " LK =", CR "SP =", " AGL=", " DEX=", CR "CHR=", " SKP=", CR "RANK: " $03.

The last three strings of attribute_labels, which print_attributes reaches again by address after printing the rank name from the record: CR "MAXCON=", CR "$=" (each followed by code $03, clear to the end of the line), and a lone CR.

Row printer for the skill list, called through the vector $47/$48 ($1968) with A = row 1-30: looks at skill pair A (+$7E + 2A); empty or not a skill (id >= 36) returns carry set. Otherwise prints the row number ($1AB4), the level in three digits and the skill name (message = skill number), carry clear.
Operand of LDY #imm at $11B2, written at $119F: the record offset of the skill pair being printed (its level is the byte after it).

Row printer for the item list, called through the vector $47/$48 ($1968) with A = slot 1-30: an empty slot returns carry set. Otherwise prints the row number ($1AB4) and the item's name (message item + 36, singular), in reverse video when the slot is the equipped weapon or armour; carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $11D5, written at entry (STA $11D6): the slot being printed, compared with the armour (+$25) and weapon (+$1F) slots.

Entry $0335, the commonest call: makes position A (1-7) of the current party ($08) the current character. Looks the record number up in the party table (party_table_ptr, leaving $68/$69 on it), then select_character. No range check: position 0 reads byte 0 of the party table.

Entry $0338. Makes record A the current character: $66/$67 = $F400 + A*256 (records 1-7 are $F500-$FBFF; record 0 would be the party page $F400), and $BB = its sex byte (+$18), which the text's his/her switch (code $0C) reads. Returns A = sex, Y = $18.
Entry $033E. Counts the items the current character carries: X = the number of non-empty slots (Z set when none) and $D1 = the last occupied slot number.

Entry $037A. Counts the current character's items whose class is in the $FF-terminated list at ($9D): for each item $0BCD points $16/$17 at its record and $0BE2 tests the class. X = the count, $D1 = the last such slot. Used by module 1 ($CAC7-$CB41).
Operand of LDX #imm at $1227, written at $1216: the counting mode, 0 for every item (count_items) or $FF for items of the listed classes (count_items_of_classes).
Operand of LDY #imm at $123F, written at $1220: the record offset of the slot being examined (+$BD..+$F7), kept here because $0BE2 uses Y; also turned into the slot number for $D1 at $1233.
Operand of LDX #imm at $1247: the running count of the item counter, cleared at $121B, raised at $123C and returned in X.

Entry $0341. Finds the current character's first empty item slot (find_item with A = 0): Y = the offset of its item byte (+$BD..+$F7) and carry clear, or Y = $FF and carry set when all 30 slots are taken.
Entry $0344. Finds item A in the current character's 30 slots: Y = the offset of its item byte and carry clear, or Y = $FF and carry set when the item is not carried.
Operand of CMP #imm at $1253, written at entry (STA $1254): the item number searched for (0 for an empty slot).

Points $16/$17 at the record of the current character's equipped armour (armour_slot_offset, then the tail of weapon_record), or of item 0 when none. No JSR or JMP to it was found in the engine or in any other part's snapshot.
Entry $034A. Points $16/$17 at the eight-byte record ($0BCD) of the current character's equipped weapon, or of Fists (item 0) when nothing is equipped. Returns A = $16, Y = $17.
Entry $0377. Equipped armour: A = Y = the record offset of the armour slot's item byte (+$BB + 2 * byte +$25), or 0 with Z set when no armour is worn.
Entry $034D. Equipped weapon: A = Y = the record offset of the weapon slot's item byte (+$BB + 2 * byte +$1F), or 0 with Z set when nothing is equipped; the count byte follows at Y+1.

Entry $0350. Reloads the equipped weapon from the clip at record offset Y (item_action_menu, the game at $A3AE). A jammed weapon (bit 7 of its count byte) gets message 152, "Your weapon is jammed.", and nothing changes. Otherwise the clip item is removed (clear_pair) and the rounds (bits 0-5) are set to the clip size, weapon record byte 4: rounds left in the weapon are lost. Assumes a weapon is equipped.
Operand of LDY #imm at $128F, written at entry (STY $1290): the record offset of the clip being used up.
Operand of LDY #imm at $1297, written at $1288: the record offset of the weapon's count byte, read back by LDY $1298 at $12A1 to store the new rounds.
Entry $0383. Makes sure the text window is open: unless $B7 is non-zero (open), text_window_open draws it; either way the print vector is set to the window's ($1DC4).

Entry $0353, and the routine behind text control code 7. Opens the text window right of the picture: frame from column 13, row 1 to column 39, row 14 (draw_frame), $B7 = $25 = 13, inside columns 14-38, then window_clear and the windowed print vector ($1DC4).

Entry $037D. Frames and clears the picture window: column 0, row 1 to column 12, row 14 (draw_frame), inside columns 1-11 cleared with colour $26 in $EB, $DF = 0 and $B8 = 1 (flags of the portrait code at $0568-$05D8, which calls this first). The caller's window ($23-$28, saved with $257E) and $EB are restored.
Clears the window between columns $25 and $26 and pixel rows 16 and 112 ($27 = $10, $28 = $70, text rows 2-13) through $22A9, which also empties the line buffer at $F49C and puts the cursor on row 2.

Entry $0398. Draws a frame with its top-left corner at column $23, row $24 and its bottom-right at column X, row Y, using the font's frame glyphs: $81 and $83 for the top corners, $85 and $7D for the bottom ones, $5C across, $84 down. Sets $26 = 39 and $28 = $78 first. Used for both windows and by the game, start-up, utils and module 4.
Operand of LDA #imm at $132D, written at $131B: the frame's left column, restored to $23 for each side glyph and (LDA $132E at $1348) for the bottom row.
Operand of CMP #imm at $1344, written at $1316: the frame's bottom row; the side glyphs are drawn until $24 reaches it.
Draws frame glyph $5C from column $23 rightwards until $23 reaches the frame's right column (the operand at $1362); at least one glyph.
Operand of CMP #imm at $1361, written at $1313: the frame's right column, where draw_frame_line stops; LDA $1362 at $1336 also puts the right-hand side glyphs there.
Entry $0356. Adds the 24-bit amount in $1C-$1E to the current character's cash (+$15..+$17); a carry out of the top byte sets the cash to $FFFFFF (16,777,215) instead of wrapping.
Sets the current character's cash (+$15..+$17) to 0. Used when cash is pooled or divided. The LDA #$FF at $1382 enters the same store for an overflowing cash_add (its BIT $00A9 skips this LDA #$00).
Stores A at ($66)+Y, Y+1 and Y+2. Besides the cash code, $0842 jumps here with A = $FF and Y = $21 to hold an overflowing experience at $FFFFFF.

Entry $0359. Looks up skill A among the current character's 30 skill pairs (+$80..+$BB, skill number then level): returns A = the level with Y = the offset of the level byte, or A = 0 (Z set) when the skill is absent.

Entry $035C. Skills page of the character screen (and the game, $8B1B): lists the current character's skills (skill_list_show) and returns its key. R starts a reorder: the skill pairs are copied to $5A00, then the player picks every skill in the new order (each pair moved to the next buffer position, move_pair_to_buffer) until the list is empty; the buffer is copied back to +$80..+$BB and the list shown again.

R on the skill list: copies the 30 skill pairs (+$80..+$BB) to $5A00-$5A3B, then lists " Reorder" until every skill has been picked; left-arrow, RETURN, space and R just list again (other keys stay inside list_choose), so left-arrow does not cancel. The empty list copies the buffer back.
Operand of LDX #imm at $13EB: the $5A00 buffer index for the next picked skill pair, cleared at $13A7 and advanced at $13F0.

Skill list: counts the current character's skill pairs with a skill number 1-35, scanning 31 pairs (+$80..+$BC, one past the 30 that skill_level reads). None returns A = $FF, carry set. Otherwise prints "LVL SKILL" (message 153) and title message A, draws the rows through print_skill_row (vector $47/$48) with R as the extra key, and returns the key from $1975.
Operand of LDA #imm at $1424, written at entry (STA $1425): the title message printed under "LVL SKILL" (0 for none, 168 for " Reorder").
Moves an item or skill pair: two bytes from ($66)+Y to $5A00+X, each source byte zeroed (move_byte_to_buffer twice). X and Y end two higher.
Moves one byte from ($66)+Y to $5A00+X and zeroes the source; X and Y end one higher.

Entry $0365. A = the class of the item whose record is at ($16): record byte 3 shifted right three times ($098A). Classes seen in the table at $3108: 1 melee, 2 pistols and thrown weapons, 3-7 the flamethrower, rifles, SMGs and assault rifles (none has 5), 8-9 rockets, 10-12 energy weapons, 13 explosives, 14 ammunition, 15 armour, 16-18 equipment and quest items.
Points $16/$17 at the record of item A ($0BCD), then falls into item_effect. Reached from use_item_charge.

Entry $0368. Runs the use effect of the item whose record is at ($16): bits 0-2 of record byte 3 index item_effect_vectors and the routine there is jumped to through $12/$13 ($1EFD, JMP ($0012)). Effect 0 is an RTS; effect 1 is the screen shake at $0746, set on the grenades, explosives and rockets (items 6-12). Of the records only item 94's (Cash, which differs between the item files) can have another: byte 3 $FB in the snapshot, effect 3, which would read code bytes after the table as the address $A02C; the loot code pays item 94 out as money (game $9263) instead of putting it in a slot.
item_effect_vectors: the use effects by number, low byte then high byte: 0 = $1474 (an RTS, no effect), 1 = $0746 (screen shake, explosion). item_effect reads the low bytes here with LDA $1469,Y.
High bytes of item_effect_vectors, read by item_effect with LDA $146A,Y.
Entry $036B. A = byte 6 of the item record at ($16): the damage dice of a weapon, the armour class of armour (equip_toggle stores it in +$1A).

Entry $036E. A = byte 4 of the item record at ($16): for a gun, its clip size (reload_weapon stores it as the rounds; 7 for the M1911A1, 18 for the VP91Z); 1 for the rockets and explosives, 40 for Matches, 0 or 1 for most other items. What the game does with it for items that are not guns was not traced (callers: the game $A4D0, $A544; the Ranger Center $81BD; module 1 $CBFD).
The RTS that ends item_record_byte6/byte4, also entry 0 of item_effect_vectors: the use effect of every item without one.

Entry $0371. Condition of a character whose CON (+$1D/+$1E) is 0 or negative: X = 5 when CON is 0; otherwise the low byte of CON is compared (unsigned) with condition_thresholds, X = 0 UNC (-1 to -10), 1 SER (-11 to -19), 2 CRT (-20 to -29), 3 MRT (-30 to -39), 4 COM (-40 to -256). Only the low byte counts, so below -256 the scale starts again (-257 gives UNC); a positive CON gives a meaningless X. roster_line_fields maps X through condition_messages. The game's end-of-game test ($7ED5-$7EFC) calls it ($7EE6) for a record that is not conscious and still counts that record as alive when X = 0 (UNC) and +$28 is 0.

condition_thresholds: low bytes of CON compared by condition_index from the top down: $D8 (-40) COM, $E2 (-30) MRT, $EC (-20) CRT, $F5 (-11) SER; the first byte, $FF, is never compared (X = 0 ends the loop).
Entry $0374. Z set when the current character's CON (+$1D/+$1E) equals MAXCON (+$1B/+$1C): fully healed. Used by $08A5 (heal one point) and module 0.

Entry $0380. Uses one charge of the item at record offset Y (the game, $8E6D and $8FAD): a count of 0 in bits 0-5 of its count byte means unlimited; otherwise the count drops by one, and the last charge removes the item, unequipping it first. Then the item's use effect runs (item_effect_of), so a grenade, explosive or rocket (effect 1, items 6-12) shakes the screen when a check square takes a charge of it; both callers are the game's check-square code (square_checks $8E6D, find_item_check $8FAD), and throwing one in combat does not come here.
Operand of ORA #imm at $14C0, written at $14B9: the new charge count, merged with the flag bits 6-7 of the count byte.
Operand of LDA #imm at $14C4, written at $14AA: the item number, whose use effect runs at the end of use_item_charge.
Operand of LDY #imm at $14D2, written at entry (STY $14D3): the record offset of the item, used to clear its slot when the last charge is gone.
Entry $0392. Copies the current character's 24-bit cash (+$15..+$17) to $1C-$1E (to print it, pool it, or test it). Leaves Y = $17.
Zeroes the pair at ($66)+Y and ($66)+Y+1 (an item number and its count byte: its callers $0F0C, $1291 and $14D4 all clear item slots); Y ends one higher.
A = the record offset of skill pair A: A*2 + $7E, so pair 1 is at +$80 and pair 30 at +$BA.
A = the record offset of item slot A: A*2 + $BB, so slot 1 is at +$BD and slot 30 at +$F7; the count byte follows.

Entry $0386. Party member A tries to unjam the item at record offset Y. The count byte (Y+1) has bit 7 set when jammed; the game writes $80 when a weapon jams ($A5B5), losing the rounds, and bits 0-5 count the failed tries here. Target 15 + 5*tries; 6 or more tries fail at once. 2d6 (under 5 fails) + IQ (+$0F) + weapon_skill_bonus must reach it. Success: "<name> unjammed the weapon.", count byte 0, roster line redrawn. Failure: "<name> can't unjam the weapon." and one more try counted, up to $85.
Operand of LDY #imm at $150D, written at $14FE: the record offset of the jammed item's count byte, read back by LDY $150E at $1543 and $1554.
Operand of LDA #imm at $154A, written at $1501: the member number, for the roster redraw after a successful unjam.
Entry $0395. Waits for a key ($24F2): carry set for left-arrow or N, otherwise carry clear with A = the key code (ASCII with bit 7 set, $D9 = Y).
Entry $038C. Copies the current character's 24-bit experience (+$21..+$23) to $1C-$1E. Used by the game ($B1B8, $B334).

Entry $038F. Pool: for every other member 1 to $07 of the current party, moves that member's whole cash to member A (cash_load, cash_clear, then cash_add on A, which saturates). It selects member A again after each move ($1596), so it returns with A selected whenever the party has another member. Used by the character screen and modules 0 and 1.
Operand of CMP #imm at $1586, written at entry (STA $1587): the member who receives the pool; LDA $1587 at $1593 selects him for each addition.
Operand of LDA #imm at $159C, written at $1583: the member counter (1 to $07) of pool_cash.

roster_party_shown: the party number ($08) whose members the roster was last drawn for, written by roster_draw ($15DC) and compared by roster_line ($1639), which redraws the whole roster when the current party differs.

Entry $0204. When the roster is shown ($6A non-zero), redraws the member numbers "1>" to "n>" down its left edge (rows 16 on, $1857 and $1861) for members 1 to $07, without highlight ($29 and $CF = 0); the game calls it at $B267 and $B41D.
Operand of LDA #imm at $15C4, written at $15B8: the member counter of roster_numbers_redraw.

Entry $028F. Draws the roster when it is shown ($6A non-zero): records the party in roster_party_shown, prints roster_header_string (party number, glyph $3C, number of parties) at column 0, row 15 and the header message 136 ("NAME AC AMM MAX CON WEAPON"), then roster_line_plain for positions 1-7, which clears the lines of absent members.
Operand of LDA #imm at $1613, written at $160D: the position counter (1-7) of roster_draw.

roster_header_string: the start of the roster header, printed by roster_draw: $01 (reverse video on), the party number in ASCII, $3C (glyph '<'), the number of parties, $00. The two digits are written each time.
The party digit of roster_header_string: '1' + $08, written by roster_draw at $15E2.
The parties digit of roster_header_string: '1' + $0B (the highest party number), written by roster_draw at $15EA.

Entry $02C9. Redraws the roster line of party member A highlighted ($CF = $FF, reverse number). view_character uses it for the member on screen ($0DFF); the game part and location modules 0-2 call it through $02C9.
Redraws the roster line of party member A plain ($CF = 0).

Entry $0297. Redraws the roster line of party member A with the current highlight $CF (the LDY $CF here is hidden behind the BIT at $1627); selects the member (select_member). Nothing when the roster is hidden ($6A = 0); the whole roster (roster_show) when it shows another party than $08. The line is row 15 + A; positions beyond $07 are only cleared (control code 3). Position 0 is not refused: it selects the record in byte 0 of the party table and would draw on row 15, the header. The game's calls at $A5BF and $A965 pass the member in a self-modified operand (hit_roll_member_op $A5BE, written at $A584; damaged_member_op $A964, written at $A861), not 0.
Operand of LDA #imm at $1648, written at $162C: the position whose line is drawn, read back at $1652 and $1668.

One roster line of the current character: number and ">" (reverse when $CF is $FF), name, AC (+$1A) at column 18; AMM at column 22: bits 0-5 of the equipped weapon's count byte when its class is in the list at $08E8 (classes 2-13: pistols, thrown, rifles, SMGs, rockets, energy weapons, explosives), and 0 when it is jammed, for Fists and melee weapons (class 1) and for classes 14-18; MAX (+$1B/+$1C) at column 25, in reverse when +$28 is non-zero; CON at column 29 (roster_con_field); the weapon at column 33 (print_weapon_name).
The CON column: a negative CON prints its condition word (condition_index, condition_messages), CON 0 prints message 132 (a space and glyph $7F, a skull), a positive CON prints the number.

condition_messages: the engine message numbers for condition_index X = 0-5: 133 UNC, 154 SER, 155 CRT, 156 MRT, 157 COM (each in reverse, codes $01/$02) and 132 (a space and the skull glyph $7F) for CON 0.

Entry $02C0 (no JSR or JMP to $02C0 was found in any part's snapshot). Prints the name of the current character's equipped weapon in the singular ($38 = 1), "Fists" (item 0) when nothing is equipped, in reverse video when the weapon's count byte has bit 7 set (jammed). The roster's WEAPON column, from column 33.

Entry $0294. Copies the 256-byte character record A over record X (record n is at $F400 + n*256); does nothing when X = 0, and checks nothing else. Leaves $66/$67 on record A and $12/$13 on record X. remove_member uses it to close up the records ($180C).

Entry $029C. Prints the current character's name (the zero-terminated string at +$00) through the current print vector ($1DE1, with $31/$32 = $66/$67). Used by text code $0B ($1FBD), by roster_line_fields, and through $029C by the game part and Party order.
Entry $02A4. Adds record A to the current party ($08): party_table_ptr, then party_add. Used by the Ranger Center ($7F8A).

Entry $02A7. Puts record A in the first free position of the party table at ($68) and adds one to $07, the current party's size, whichever table ($68) points at. No check for a full party: with positions 1-7 taken, party_size returns Y = 8, so the record lands in byte 8 of the table (the party's column) and $07 becomes 8.
Entry $02AB. A = the number of members of party A (party_table_ptr, then party_size).
Counts the members of the party table at ($68), positions 1-7 up to the first 0: A = the count, Y = count + 1 (the first free position).

Entry $029F. Points $68/$69 at the table of party A (0-3): $F400 + party_table_offsets[A], i.e. $F400, $F40E, $F41C or $F42A. Each table is 14 bytes: positions 1-7 at +1..+7 hold record numbers. Returns X = A.
party_table_offsets: low bytes of the four party tables in page $F4: $00, $0E, $1C, $2A.

Entry $02AE. Waits for a member number: keys 1-8 are accepted when the number is at most $07 (the party size) and returned in A; left-arrow returns 0. Used for "Who wants it?" and by the game, the Ranger Center, Order and modules 0-2.

Entry $02B1. A = the party (0-3) whose table holds record A, searching tables 0 to 3 in turn; a record in no party also gives 3, the last table searched. $68/$69 are put back on the current party ($08).
Operand of LDA #imm at $17A3, written at entry (STA $17A4): the record number find_party_of looks for.
Operand of LDA #imm at $17AA, written at $179D: the party being searched, returned by LDA $17AB at $17B7.
Entry $02B4. Carry clear when record A is at one of positions 1-7 of the party table at ($68), with Y = its position; carry set when absent. A = 0 matches an empty position.

Entry $02B7. Shows the roster again ($6A = 1) and clears $C9, the flag $1EA9 sets when it clears roster rows 18-22 (message 169) to print text at the bottom of the screen. When lines have scrolled since the last key press ($AF non-zero), $21E8 first shows "(RETURN)" on the bottom line and waits. Then roster_draw, which draws members 1 to $07 and clears the other lines: with $07 = 0 it clears every member line, which the Order program uses ($CA17-$CA1E). Keeps A.
Entry $02BD. Z set when the current character's CON (+$1D/+$1E) is exactly 0, which the roster shows as a skull.
Entry $02BA. Selects party member A (select_member) and tests is_conscious.
Entry $02C3. Carry clear when the current character's CON (+$1D/+$1E) is 1 or more; carry set when it is 0 or negative (unconscious, worse, or dead).

Entry $02C6. Removes party member A (a position, 1-7) of the current party; the body is at $1800-$1856. Records above the member's record move down one (copy_character), the members after it in the party table move up one position and position 7 is cleared, $07 (party size) and $0A (characters in use) drop by one, and in every party table 0 to $0B a record number at or above the removed one is lowered by one. The position is kept in the operand at $1801. Nothing checks that the position holds a member, and $68/$69 is left on party 0's table.

Operand of the LDY #imm at $1800, written at run time: the slot (1-7) of the current group that remove_member ($17F8) empties, then the group counter of its renumbering loop ($1837-$1854), from $0B down to 0.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $180F, written at run time: the record number while the records above the removed one are copied a page down ($1807-$1816, $171B), then ($1819) the removed character's number n; the loop at $183F lowers every group member numbered n or more by one.
Puts the text cursor at column 0 of roster line A: row $0F+A into $24, 0 into $23 (the roster's lines are rows 16-22). Called by the roster drawing at $15BB and $164A.

Prints A as a one-digit number followed by '>', the start of a roster line: selects direct output ($1DB9), sets the number width $30 to 1, prints with $1C83, then '>' through $1F03. Called from $15C1 and $166B.

(= $02CF) Reads page A (0-7) of the saved game from track 35, logical sector 7-A, to $F400+A*$100 (the address from $1201), one sector through $27E8, which retries after an error message and returns once the transfer has worked. X = 0 is the loader's one-sector read; entered at $1875, behind the BIT at $1874, X is 2, a write.

(= $02D2) Writes page A (0-7) of the saved game, $F400+A*$100, to track 35, logical sector 7-A: the second entry of $1872 (the BIT at $1874 hides LDX #$02), loader operation 2. $18EA calls it for all eight pages.
Operand of the SBC #imm at $188B, written at run time ($187A): the save page A, so that X = 7 - A, the logical sector on track 35. 7 in play-map: the last page written.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1890, written at run time ($1877): the loader operation handed to $27E8, 0 (read one sector) from $1872, 2 (write) from $1875. 2 in play-map.

(= $02CC and $02D5) Waits until side 1 is in the drive: A = 1, then the side check $1897. Called through $02D5 before a program is loaded from side 1 (the game's Radio $880F and death branch $7EFE, the start-up $81E8 and $8293, the utilities $821B, the radio $8196, the Ranger Center $7EF1, module 3 $CA15) and by the Save command before it saves ($882A). Nothing calls $02CC.

(= $02DB) Waits until disk side A (1-4) is in the drive: reads track 35 logical sector 8 to $5A00 ($FD19) and wants $5AFD = $ED, $5AFE = $CC and $5AFF = A; on a mismatch prints 'INSERT SIDE n. (RETURN)' at the left of the bottom line (engine messages $A6, $A7), waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow ($2501, whose carry it ignores), redraws the menu bar ($1B36) and tries again. A read error does not reach that prompt: $FD19 reads through disk_io ($03AA, $27E8), which prints its own error message and retries until the read succeeds, returning carry clear, so the BCS at $18A9 is never taken. Returns carry clear, $6B = A. $ED is 0 in play; the start-up sets it to $D7 only around its side-1 check before loading Utils from the master (startup $81E4-$81ED), so masters are refused everywhere else. Also called by $27C3 with a directory entry's side.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $18D4, written at run time ($189B): the side asked for as an ASCII digit ('1'-'4'), printed between 'INSERT SIDE ' and '. (RETURN)'.

(= $02D8) Saves the game state to the disk in the drive, with no side check of its own: copies zero page $02-$0F to $F478-$F485, takes the checksum of the eight pages $F400-$FBFF ($1918) into $F4FF, scrambles the pages with it ($1944), writes them to track 35 logical sectors 7 down to 0 ($1875), then unscrambles them again. Returns carry clear. The Save command asks for side 1 first ($882A); the Radio saves to whatever side is in the drive ($880C) and only then asks for side 1.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1909, written at run time ($1903): the page (0-7) that save_game's write loop has reached.

(= $04EA) Checksum of the saved game in $F400-$FBFF: for every page and every offset Y = 0-$FE, sum = sum + byte + Y (with the carry of the first add), eight bits; byte $FF of each page is left out. Returns the sum in A (also left in $1926). save_game stores it at $F4FF and scrambles with it; the start-up unscrambles a loaded save with $F4FF and compares this sum with it (startup $8321-$832D). Selects each page with $1201, so $66/$67 and $BB change.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1925, written at run time: the running checksum of $1918 (zeroed at $191A, kept at the end of each page at $1934, read back as the result at $1940). $C7 in play-map.
Operand of the ADC #imm at $192D, written at run time ($192A): the offset Y in the page, added to the checksum after the byte itself.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1937, written at run time ($191D): the page (0-7) the checksum has reached.

(= $04E7) Scrambles or unscrambles the saved game in place with the key in A (the same operation both ways): each byte at offset Y = 0-$FE of the eight pages $F400-$FBFF is EORed with (2*Y mod 256) EOR A. Byte $FF of each page is not touched, so the key kept at $F4FF survives. Selects each page with $1201, so $66/$67 and $BB change.
Operand of the EOR #imm at $1955, written at run time ($1944): the scrambling key passed in A, the checksum. $C7 in play-map.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $195E, written at run time ($1949): the page (0-7) being scrambled.

Calls the list's per-item routine through the vector $47/$48 (JMP ($0047)) with the item number in A and $D0. The routine prints the item on list line $50 and returns carry clear, or carry set to leave the item off the page. Used by $19ED and $1A3A.

Item number shown on each line 0-8 of the list page, nine bytes $196B-$1973: written by $19ED and $1A3A as they fill the lines, read by $1975 to turn a digit key into the item. The tenth byte, $1974, is read and written by no code found (0 in both snapshots).

(= $039B) Waits for a choice from the list page: keys 1-9 pick a line shown (A = that line's item from $196B, also in $49; the line in $51; carry clear); other digits and keys are ignored. When the list is longer than a page ($19E3), I or DEL (or code $8B) show the previous page, K, either cursor key or C= the next. Carry set with A = $FF for the left-arrow key (cancel), $FE for the extra key in $BE ('R' at $1092 and $1436, 'P' in module 1; the Ranger Center stores $92, which no key gives, at $8400, and the game's lists and module 2's leave $BE as it was), $FD for RETURN or space.

Carry set when the list fits on one page: the item count $4E (most callers keep it one above the number of items, as at game $9194; module 1's buy list, $CBD7, and the Ranger Center's skill list, $8412-$8428, keep the number itself) is no more than the page length $4F. Carry clear when paging is possible.

(= $03A4) Shows a page of the list starting at item $4A: sets up the page ($1A7A), then for items $4A, $4A+1, ... (after $4D-1 back to 1) records the item for the next line in $196B and calls the per-item routine ($1968), which prints it on line $50 or declines; stops when the $4F lines are full or every item has been offered, blanking the lines left. $4B = the last item offered, $D0 = the item; ends with the MORE line ($1A89).

Shows the page before the current one: from the bottom line (8, fixed) upwards, offers the items before $4A (below 1 back to $4D-1) to the per-item routine until line 0 is filled; $4B = the item on the bottom line, $4A = the item on line 0. It has no stop of its own: $19E3 lets it run only when $4E is above $4F, that is with more items than lines, or with as many where $4E is kept one above the number of items (most callers). Ends with the MORE line ($1A89).
Sets up a list page: first list row $42 = 4, page length $4F = 9 lines (rows 4-12), cursor column $23 = the window's left edge $25, normal video ($1FA9). The cursor row is left as it was.

Prints the line under the list, row $42+$4F (13), from the window's left edge: 'MORE' and an arrow in inverse (text at $1AAB) when the item count $4E is above $4F+1, otherwise just clears that line ($03).
Text printed under a list longer than a page ($1A89): $03 (clear to the end of the line), $01 (inverse), 'MORE', glyph $5E (a two-headed vertical arrow in this font), $02 (normal), $00 (end).

(= $03A7) Starts list line $50 for the per-item routine: prints the line's digit ($50+1) at column $25, row $42+$50, then '>', or '_' when the item $D0 is the marked one ($D1), clears to the end of the line and prints a space, leaving the cursor where the item's text goes. Selects direct output.

(= $03A1) Flashes the chosen list line $51: inverts it from column 14 to the window's right edge three times with a pause after each ($1AEB), so it ends inverted; normal video afterwards. The game calls it after acting on a choice (game $927C, $929D), straight after the choice at $B5B2 and $B710, and at $8B35; the engine ($109B, $13E2), modules 1 ($CB29, $CC0F) and 2 ($CB16, $CB3E) and the Ranger Center ($814B, $816A) call it too.
Inverts list line $51 (row $42+$51) from column 14, the text window's left edge inside its frame, to the window's right edge $26 ($226B with $29 = $FF), then pauses ($242B, A = $A0).
(= $039E) Address of record A of a table: $16/$17 = $45/$46 + A * $4C, the base and the record size set by the caller; also returned in A (low) and Y (high).

(= $02E4) Waits for one of the keys in the zero-terminated list at ($31/$32) (codes with bit 7 set, as $2514 returns them): returns its index in A and Y; A = Y = $FF for the left-arrow key (cancel). Other keys are ignored.
Low byte of the LDA $FFFF,Y operand at $1B26, written at run time ($1B17): the address of the caller's key list, from $31.
High byte of the LDA $FFFF,Y operand at $1B26, from $32 ($1B1C): with $1B27 it points the LDA at the key list wait_listed_key searches.

(= $02E7) Draws the menu bar on the bottom line (row 23, columns 0-39): the text of menu $3B in inverse, the rest of the line cleared and inverted to a solid bar, then falls into $1B5C to show the selected item $39 in normal video. Keeps the text window; leaves direct output selected (through $1DCF), which is why $20F9 selects word wrap again after it.

(= $02E1) Draws menu item $39 on the bar in normal video (selected); entered at $1B5F (behind the BIT at $1B5E) in inverse video (not selected). Finds the item's column with $1B88 and reprints its word at row $3D.
Second entry of $1B5C (the BIT at $1B5E hides its LDX #$FF): X = $FF, so the menu item is drawn in inverse, as part of the bar, when the selection moves off it.

Finds menu item $39 in the text of menu $3B ($1BB1): items are words separated by spaces; $3C = the offset of item $39's first letter, which is also its column on the bar. With $39 above $3A (the last visible item) $3C ends at the zero after the visible items, where the hot keys of the hidden items begin.
Points $31/$32 at the text of menu $3B: word $3B of the table at ($3E/$3F).

(= $02DE) Handles key $18 on the menu bar: ',' and '.' move the selection $39 left and right (wrapping), RETURN runs the selected item ($1C55), an item's first letter selects and runs it, and the hot keys after the bar's text select and run the hidden items numbered from $3A+1. In play the game's bar 'Use Enc Order Disband View Save Radio' has hidden keys I, K, J, L, left arrow and space (text at $5BAB, handlers at game $7F18): the moves are hidden menu items. Returns at once for no key or any other key.
Runs item $39 of menu $3B: the handler is word $39 of the table whose address is word $3B of ($40/$41); it is written into the JSR at $1C71 and called, then the bar is redrawn ($1B36).

Low byte of the JSR operand at $1C71, written at run time ($1C68): the handler of the menu item being run. The JSR holds $7E7E in play-map, the Ranger Center's Start (item 2 of its table at ranger $7E69), the last item run before the snapshot; $0201 at the hand-over.
High byte of the JSR operand at $1C71, written at run time ($1C6E): with $1C72, the address run_menu_item calls.
(= $02ED) Prints the 24-bit number in $1C-$1E in decimal, right-aligned in $30 columns (leading zeros as spaces), through the current output.
(= $02F0) Prints the 24-bit number in $1C-$1E in decimal without leading zeros, through the current output.
(= $02F3) Prints A in decimal, right-aligned in $30 columns (leading zeros as spaces).
(= $02F6) Prints A in decimal without leading zeros.
(= $032C) Converts A to BCD: $1C = A, $1D = $1E = 0, then $243B leaves eight BCD digits in $1F-$22. Entered at $1C91 the high byte comes from X.
Converts the 16-bit number X:A to BCD: $1C = A, $1D = X, $1E = 0, then $243B (digits in $1F-$22).
(= $02FC) Prints the 16-bit number X:A in decimal, right-aligned in $30 columns.
Prints the BCD number in $1F-$22 right-aligned in $30 columns: pad character $2E = space, then $1CB1.
(= $02F9) Prints the 16-bit number X:A in decimal without leading zeros.
Prints the BCD number in $1F-$22 without leading zeros: width $30 = 8, pad $2E = 0 (nothing), then $1CB1.

(= $0329) Prints the eight BCD digits in $1F-$22 (most significant first, $22) through the current output: only the last $30 digit positions are printed, leading zeros become the pad character $2E (0 prints nothing), and the last digit is always printed. $2D and $2F are its working flags.
Prints both BCD digits of A through $1CD4, high digit first.
Prints one BCD digit A (0-9) for $1CB1: position $2F counts down from 8; a leading zero while $2D is set becomes the pad $2E; positions above $30 are not printed.

Unreached entry of the line input: LDA #$FF, then the BIT at $1CFF hides $1D00's LDA, so $2C = $FF (digits only) and X = $FF. No code in any part's snapshot calls or stores $1CFD; the bytes are left undecoded.
(= $030E) The line input $1D06 with X = $FF written to the flag at $1D2C, which chooses between two identical JSR $2514 calls, so it behaves like $1D06.

(= $02EA) Reads a line of typed text into the buffer at ($31/$32), at most $35 characters (13 for a Ranger's name, ranger $836C; 16 for a typed word, game $892F), from the text cursor with a blinking '_'. Zeroes bytes 0-$35 first. Key codes $A0 and up are stored without bit 7 and echoed ($1F00), so F1, F3, F5 and F7 ($F1-$F7) type a lowercase q, s, u, w; DEL deletes, RETURN accepts (trailing spaces removed; A = 0, length in $33), the left-arrow key cancels (A = $FF).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $1D2B, written at run time ($1D0B): X on entry to the line input, 0 from $1D06 or $FF from $1D00. It picks between the JSR $2514 at $1D35 and the identical one at $1D2F, so it changes nothing.
For an empty line ($33 = 0) Y becomes $FF here, so the trim starts at byte 255 of the buffer; if that byte is a space it is zeroed and the scan goes on downwards, leaving a bogus length in $33.
Only spaces were typed: Y goes from 0 to $FF here, so byte 255 of the buffer is examined, and zeroed if it is a space.
Pause between the input cursor's blinks: $242B with A = $30.
Draws the input cursor '_' at the text cursor and steps the cursor back; entered at $1DAC (behind the BIT at $1DAB) it draws a space instead. Normal video.
Erases the input cursor: prints a space at the text cursor in normal video and steps the cursor back ($1DAE).
(= $02FF) Selects direct output: the JMP at $1DF8 (print_char) goes to $1F03, which draws each character at once.
(= $0302) Selects word-wrapped output: the JMP at $1DF8 goes to $1F92, which collects a line in the buffer at $F49C and wraps whole words at the window's right edge.
(= $0277) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) at the text cursor; selects direct output ($1DB9), which stays selected. Returns X/Y = the cursor.
(= $0274) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) at column X, row Y; selects direct output ($1DB9), which stays selected.
(= $026F) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) at the text cursor; selects word-wrapped output ($1DC4), which stays selected.
(= $026C) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) at column X, row Y; selects word-wrapped output ($1DC4), which stays selected.
(= $0305) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) at column X, row Y through the current output.

(= $0308) Prints the zero-terminated string at ($31/$32) from the text cursor through the current output; control codes act as in that output's table ($1F42 for $1F03, $1F64 for $1F92, which differ at $08 and $0D). Leaves $31/$32 past the zero and X/Y = the cursor.
(= $030B) Prints a space through the current output.
(= $0323) Prints character A through the current output: a JMP whose target $1DB9 sets to $1F03 (direct) and $1DC4 to $1F92 (word-wrapped).
Low byte of the JMP at $1DF8, the current output: $03 (to $1F03, direct) written by $1DB9, $92 (to $1F92, word-wrapped) written by $1DC4. The hand-over holds a JMP to $1DF8 itself.
High byte of the JMP at $1DF8: $1F for both outputs, written by $1DC0 and $1DCB all the same.
(= $0317) Prints message A of the current map's text block (selected by $1E4F from the word at ($61)) through the current output.
(= $0311) Prints message A of the packed text block at $43/$44 through the current output: finds it ($1E0E) and decodes it character by character ($28F4) up to its end code.

(= $0314) Finds message A in the packed text block at $43/$44: copies the base to $52/$53 (the alphabet), points $31/$32 at group A/4 through the word table at base+$3C (offsets from the table), then decodes and discards A AND 3 messages ($28F4). The bit reader is then at message A. The INC $32 at $1E26 would serve groups from 128 on, which an 8-bit message number never reaches.
Operand of the ADC #imm at $1E32, written at run time ($1E1C): the high byte of the message table's address (base+$3C), added to the group's offset from that table.
Number of messages find_message ($1E0E) still has to skip in the group, 1-3 (written at $1E3E, counted down at $1E48). A variable between two routines, not code.
(= $031A) Selects the current map's text block: $43/$44 = the first word of the map's header at ($61/$62) ($4C00 in play-map, whose word points at the world map's messages at $5123). Keeps A.
(= $031D) Shows message A of the current map's text block in the message area ($1E4F, then $1E60).

(= $0326) Shows message A of the text block at $43/$44 in the message area, rows 18-22 across the whole screen, word-wrapped, continuing from where the last one stopped (cursor kept in $1E78/$1E7C), with a '(RETURN)' pause once six lines have gone by since a key was read ($B0 set, $AF). If the roster is up ($6A) and the area has not been cleared since it was drawn ($C9 = 0), clears it first ($1EA9). Keeps the window and $A8 (slow scroll off meanwhile).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1E77, written at run time ($1E99): the column where show_message ($1E60) left the cursor, where the next message continues. 0 in play-map.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1E7B, written at run time ($1E9E): the row (18-22) where show_message left off. $16 (row 22) in play-map, $12 (row 18) at the hand-over.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $1E92, written at run time ($1E60): the message show_message prints. $18 in play-map.
Clears the message area through $1EAE unless it is already clear ($C9 set).

(= $0320) Clears the message area (rows 18-22, columns 0-39) by printing engine message $A9 ({03} and a new line four times, then {03}), after a '(RETURN)' prompt ($21E8) if lines were printed since a key was last read ($AF); then $AF = 0 and $C9 = 1 (area clear). Keeps the window, $A8 and $43/$44; leaves direct output selected.
Sets the text cursor: column $23 = X, row $24 = Y.
Steps the string pointer $31/$32 on by one byte.
(= $04DE) Sets the count $38 to 1, so texts take their singular forms (control code $0A).
Jumps through the vector $12/$13 (JMP ($0012)): $1F39 calls the print handler with it; $1466 jumps through it too.
(= $027C) Prints character A at column X, row Y, direct output.

(= $027F) Prints character A at the text cursor, direct: codes $00-$0F are controls dispatched through the table at $1F42, codes $10 and up are drawn ($1F86). Skips everything while $A1 is set; runs the his/her, three-way and plural filters first. Returns X/Y = the cursor.

Shared body of $1F03 and $1F92 with the control table in $12/$13: nothing while $A1 is non-zero; otherwise A passes the filters $2099 ($BC), $20C3 ($CB) and $2063 ($B3), and its handler (entry A, or 16 for codes $10 and up) runs via $1EFD. Then the scroll-speed keys ($253A) and X/Y = the cursor.

Handlers for direct output, 17 words read at $1F2D: control codes $00-$0F, then entry 16 for every code from $10 (draw the glyph, $1F86). $00 nothing, $01 inverse on, $02 inverse off, $03 clear to end of line, $04 clear the window, $05 wait for RETURN, space or back-arrow ($2501), $06 '(RETURN)' prompt, $07 open the text window ($12B0), $08 nothing, $09 tab, $0A singular/plural, $0B name, $0C his/her, $0D new line, $0E three-way choice, $0F the count $38.

Handlers for word-wrapped output, 17 words read at $1F2D: as at $1F42 except $08 draws the buffered line ($200C), $0D ends the line with word wrap ($1FFB) and entry 16 puts the glyph in the line buffer ($1FEA).
Control table entry 16 for direct output: draws glyph A-$20 at the cursor ($2217) and moves the cursor one column right.
Prints character A at column X, row Y, word-wrapped: the counterpart of $1F00 for $1F92. No caller found in any part's snapshot.
(= $0284) Prints character A word-wrapped: as $1F03, but with the control table at $1F64, whose printable entry stores glyphs in the line buffer at $F49C and wraps whole words.
Control code $0F: prints the count $38 in decimal (0 printed as 1), as in the combat text 'killing ... {0F} of them'.
Not a variable: the disassembler made this symbol from the BIT $1FA0 at $10CF and $1275, where the BIT only hides an LDY #$1F (the skip idiom). The byte is the operand of the BNE at $1F9F.
(= $0287) Inverse video on: $29 = $FF, which the glyph drawing EORs in. Control code $01. The BIT at $1FA8 hides $1FA9's LDA.
(= $028C) Inverse video off: $29 = 0. Control code $02. Returns A = 0.
Control code $09 in a plain string: moves the cursor right by the next byte of the string and skips that byte; reads ($31/$32), so it only works in strings printed by $1DE1.
Control code $0B: prints the current character's name, the string at the start of the record at ($66/$67) ($173A), keeping $31/$32.

Control code $06: prints '(RETURN)' at column 23, row 13 through the current output (text at $1FDE: the prompt, $08, $05, $03), waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow, then clears the row from the cursor: in word-wrapped output the $08 has sent the cursor back to the window's left edge, so the prompt is wiped; in direct output it stays. Keeps the window and $31/$32.
Text of control $06's prompt ($1FC3): '(RETURN)', $08 (draw a word-wrapped line), $05 (wait for RETURN, space or back-arrow), $03 (clear to the end of the line), $00 (end).

Control table entry 16 for word-wrapped output: stores glyph A-$20 in the line buffer at $F49C + column; moves the cursor right, or when the column is past the window's right edge $26, wraps the line ($1FFB).

(= $0264) Ends a word-wrapped line, as control code $0D of word-wrapped output and when a glyph runs past the right edge ($1FF6): draws the buffered line ($200C: up to the cursor, or to the last space when the line overflowed), then a new line ($20F9), keeping the column $200C left after any word carried over. Nothing while $A1 is set.

Control code $08 for word-wrapped output: draws the line buffer from the window's left edge up to the cursor, or, when the cursor has run past the right edge, up to the last space; the word cut off there moves to the start of the buffer and the cursor follows it (otherwise back to the left edge); the rest of the buffer is zeroed.
Operand of the CPX #imm at $202E, written at run time ($201E): the column of the line break draw_buffered_line found; drawing stops there and the carried word starts after it ($2034).

Control code $0A: starts a singular/plural choice ($B3 = 1), as in 'Kni{0A}fe{0A}ves{0A}': the text up to the next $0A is printed when the count $38 is 1, the text up to the third $0A when it is not. Can hold a $0E choice inside it.

Filter for control code $0A (active while $B3 is set): returns A, or 0 to print nothing, by the count $38 (1 = singular) and the state at $2064; the third $0A ends the choice. Hands the result on to $20C3 when a $0E choice is active ($CB), so a him/her/it choice can sit inside it.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $2063: the state of the singular/plural choice, 0 in its first text, 1 in its second ($207A); back to 0 when the third $0A ends it ($208F).
Control code $0C: starts a his/her choice ($BC = 1), as in 'h{0C}is{0C}er{0C}': the first text is printed when $BB is 0, the second when it is not.

Filter for control code $0C (active while $BC is set): keeps A or returns 0 by $BB, byte +$18 of the record $1201 last selected (0 prints the first text: 'his', 'him'; so 0 is male), with the state at $209A; the third $0C ends the choice.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $2099: the state of the his/her choice, 0 in its first text, 1 in its second ($20A8); back to 0 at the third $0C ($20BA).
Not a variable: the disassembler made this symbol from the BIT $20A9 at $1DAB, which only hides the LDA #$20 of $1DAC. The byte is the operand of the INC $209A at $20A8.
Control code $0E: starts a three-way choice ($CB = 1): of the three texts between four $0E codes the one numbered $CA (0-2) is printed; the combat texts use it for him/her/it.

Filter for control code $0E (active while $CB is set): keeps A only while the text number (state at $20C4, 0-2) equals $CA, returns 0 otherwise; the fourth $0E ends the choice. Called twice for a character inside a $0A choice ($1F1A, $2077), harmlessly: the second call sees the first one's result.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $20C3: the number (0-2) of the text of the three-way choice being read, stepped by each $0E ($20D7), back to 0 at the fourth ($20F5).

(= $0267) Control code $0D, new line: in slow-scroll mode ($A8) first pauses by the speed $0F; with $B0 set asks '(RETURN)' ($21E8) once six lines have gone by since a key was read ($AF); then the cursor goes to the window's left edge and down a row, or on the window's last row the window scrolls up eight pixel lines (in one step, or by the speed $0F in slow mode).
Scrolls the text window (columns $25-$26, pixel lines $27-$28) up by $0F pixel lines, copying each line of cells, then clears the bottom $0F lines; first waits $C0 animation ticks ($0551).

Operand of the LDY #imm at $216F, written at run time: the pixel line copied from, the window's top $27 plus the step $0F at first ($216C), then one line further per pass ($2196) until it reaches the bottom $28.
X = $26 - $25: the window's width less one, the cell count for a loop that runs to X = -1.
Points $12/$13 at the window's left edge on the pixel line held in the operand at $21CA (the scroll's destination line), via $21CB.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $21C9, written at run time: the pixel line copied to, from the window's top $27 ($2166) downwards, one per pass ($2199, $21B9).
Points $12/$13 at pixel line Y of the bitmap, at the window's left column $25.
Steps per eight-line scroll for the speed $0F = 0-6: 8, 8, 4, 4, 2, 2, 1 (read at $2143).
Pixel lines per scroll step for the speed $0F = 0-6: 1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 8 (read at $2149 into $0F for the scroll); with $21D3 the product is always 8.

Pause before a new line in slow-scroll mode by the speed $0F = 0-6 ($20FF): $FF, $01, $C0, $01, $C0, $01, $01 rounds of a short delay ($242B, A = $0B) and three animation ticks. Not monotonic: speeds 2 and 4 wait far longer than 1 and 3.
Asks '(RETURN)' in inverse at the left of the bottom line (text at $220A), waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow, then redraws the menu bar ($1B36). Keeps the window and $31/$32.
Text of the bottom-line prompt ($21E8): $03 (clear to the end of the line), $01 (inverse), '(RETURN)', $02 (normal), $05 (wait for RETURN, space or back-arrow), $00 (end).

Draws glyph A (a character code less $20; the font at $C600 holds 102, codes $20-$85, up to $C92F) at the text cursor without moving it: copies its eight bytes from $C600+A*8 into the bitmap cell, EORed with $29 (inverse), and sets the cell's colour in the screen matrix to $EB. Nothing past the window's right edge $26.
Low byte of the LDA $C600,Y operand at $2258, written at run time ($2233): with $225A, the address of the glyph being drawn, $C600 + glyph*8.
High byte of the LDA $C600,Y operand at $2258, built in place: the glyph number's top bits rolled in ($222A), plus $C6 ($223B).
Control code $03: clears the current row from the cursor to the window's right edge (cells zeroed, colour $EB) without moving the cursor. Normal video afterwards.
Inverts the current row from the cursor to the window's right edge, EORing each cell with $29, and sets the colours to $EB: $2265's loop with the AND at $2291 turned into an EOR.
This instruction's opcode is written at run time ($226D): AND $29 ($25) when clear_to_eol clears the cells, EOR $29 ($45) when invert_to_eol inverts them.
(= $025C) Control code $04: clears the text window (rows $27/8 to $28/8-1, columns $25-$26), puts the cursor at its top left and empties the line buffer. Normal video.
(= $04ED) Empties the word-wrap line buffer: zeroes $F49C-$F4C4 (41 bytes, one per column).

(= $025F) Draws map tile A at column X, pixel line Y: two by two character cells ($22EA), with the I/O area banked out and interrupts off ($25AD, $274E) to read the tile set at $D000-$DD7F. Returns X/Y = the text cursor.
Returns the text cursor in X (column $23) and Y (row $24).

Draws tile A at column $36, pixel line $37: the tile's 32 bytes at $D000+A*32 (four cells: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right) and its four colour bytes at $DC00+A*4 into the screen matrix. Cells outside columns 1-36 or pixel lines 8-135 are skipped. Called with the I/O area banked out.

Draws one cell of a tile at column Y: eight bytes from the tile data (X counts through them), EORed with $29, and the colour byte at ($14). The instruction here is rewritten by $22EA: BIT (draw) or JMP $237F (row clipped). Skips columns outside 1-36.
Low byte of the LDA $D0E0,X operand at $2367, written at run time ($22FF): the low byte of $D000 + tile*32, the tile's graphics.
High byte of the LDA $D0E0,X operand at $2367, built in place at $22F0-$2307: the tile number's top bits, plus $D0.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $2378, written at run time ($235A): the column of the cell being drawn, where its colour byte goes in the screen matrix row ($E9).
Skips a tile cell that is clipped: steps the colour pointer $14 by one and the data index X by 8 as if it had been drawn.
Points $12/$13 at pixel line Y of the bitmap (column 0): the row's address from the tables at $049F/$04B7 plus Y AND 7.
Moves $12/$13 on by 8 bytes, to the next character cell of the bitmap.
Adds column Y's offset (Y*8, from the tables at $044F/$0477) to the bitmap pointer $12/$13.
Points $E9/$EA at the screen matrix row holding pixel line Y ($23C3 with Y/8), keeping Y.
(= $0502) Points $E9/$EA at text row Y (0-23) of the screen matrix at $5C00, from the tables at $23CE and $23E6.
Low bytes of the addresses of the 24 screen matrix rows, $5C00 + row*40 for rows 0-23, read by $23C3; the high bytes follow at $23E6.
High bytes ($5C-$5F) of the addresses of the 24 screen matrix rows, read by $23C3.
(= $023F) Absolute value: A becomes -A when it is negative (bit 7 set). Continues into $2400.
Compare the zero-terminated byte strings at ($31) and ($16), at most 256 bytes: A = 0 (Z set) when they match up to a shared 0, A = $FF when a byte differs. Y = the index reached. Entry $024F.

Calls the sound player $C993 with X = $0B: record 1 at $C9C7 (frequency $2000, pulse width $06A4, sustain 6), whose final control byte $A4 has the gate bit clear, so as written it starts no note. Entry $0232; the game ($92BC), the Ranger Center ($8188) and modules 1 ($CC52) and 2 ($CAB5) call it after printing a message, and module 1 also at $CC2D, just before printing one (message 8, $CC33-$CC35).
RTS on its own: jump-table entry $0257 lands here, so a call to $0257 returns at once.
Busy-wait X rounds of delay_a with A = $FF, about 166,000 cycles (a sixth of a second) a round; X = 0 gives 256 rounds. Returns A = 0, X = 0. Entry $0237.

Busy-wait: an outer count from A down to 1, each step counting its own value down in a five-cycle SBC/BNE loop, A*(A+1)/2 turns in all; A = 0 returns at once. Returns A = 0; X, Y kept. Entry $04F0; newline's slow-scroll pause waits delay_a(11) per round ($2107, the rounds from $21E1); a scroll step waits $C0 animation ticks instead ($215F).

Convert the 24-bit number at $1C (low), $1D, $1E to eight BCD digits at $1F (lowest pair) to $22: for X = 7 down to 0, subtract 10^X (pow10_lo/mid/hi) while it fits and add the matching BCD step (bcd_step_0-3) in decimal mode. Leaves $1C-$1E = 0. Called by the number printers $1C77, $1C7D, $1C99.
Low bytes of 10^X for X = 0-7 (1, 10, ..., 10,000,000): 01 0A 64 E8 10 A0 40 80; binary_to_bcd compares and subtracts with them.
BCD added to $1F (digits 1 and 10) each time 10^X is subtracted: 01 for X = 0, 10 for X = 1, 0 for the rest.
BCD added to $20 (hundreds and thousands): 01 for X = 2, 10 for X = 3, 0 for the rest.
BCD added to $21 (ten thousands and hundred thousands): 01 for X = 4, 10 for X = 5.
BCD added to $22 (millions and ten millions): 01 for X = 6, 10 for X = 7; the code that follows at $24C4 is random_1_to_a.
Random number from 1 to A: keeps A as the bound in rnd_bound and calls random_byte again while the result is not below it, then adds 1; A = 0 returns 0 at once. Entry $0242.
Operand of CMP #: the bound random_1_to_a was called with, written at $24C4 (100 in play-map); the loop from here draws until the byte is below it, then adds 1.
Roll one die, 1 to 6: random_byte AND 7, drawing again on 6 or 7, plus 1. Entry $023A.

Random byte taken from the clock, not a sequence: increments rnd_seed, then A = raster line ($D012) + CIA 1 timer A low byte ($DC04) + seed + carry, stored back as the seed. read_key calls it on every poll, so key timing stirs it.
Operand of ADC #: random_byte's seed, incremented at $24E3 and replaced by each result, so the next call adds the last one in.
Wait for a key: polls read_key until it returns a code; A = the code (bit 7 set, from the table at $C953), carry set if it was back-arrow ($9B), clear otherwise. Entry $022F.

Wait to go on: clears the pending key $EC, then takes keys (wait_key) until RETURN ($8D) or SPACE ($A0), returning carry clear, or back-arrow, returning carry set; other keys are ignored. Entry $03EF; printer control code 5 runs it (table at $1F42).

Poll for a key without waiting: stirs random_byte, lets speed_keys take a cursor key, then takes $EC (0 if none), clearing $EC, $AF and $B5 when a key was there; waits delay_a(4) and calls $05C5, the picture animation tick (nothing while $AC is 0). Returns the code in A and $18. Entry $022A.

Scroll-speed keys: when $A8 is set and a key is pending in $EC, CRSR down ($8A) lowers $0F, not below 0, and CRSR right ($95; C= gives the same code) raises it, at most 6, and the key is used up; other keys stay pending. $0F indexes the scroll tables at $21D3/$21DA. The printer calls this for every character ($1F3C).

Tail exit: a routine that began with JSR push_zp23 ends with JMP here; pull_zp23 puts $23-$28 back and the RTS returns from that routine to its caller. Entry $0254; $1E60 and $1EAE are two that end this way.

Pull six bytes from under the return address into $28, $27, ..., $23: the text cursor ($23 column, $24 row) and window ($25 left and $26 right column, $27 top and $28 bottom in pixel lines), undoing push_zp23. A, X, Y changed. Entry $024C.

Push the text cursor and window, $23 to $28, onto the stack beneath the return address, so a routine can print elsewhere and put them back with pull_zp23 (or end with JMP pull_zp23_and_return). A, X, Y changed. Entry $0247.

Keep the text bit pointer $31/$32 in saved_bit_ptr_lo/hi, the operands of restore_bit_pointer: one saved value, not a stack. Used around printing a name in a message ({0B}, $1FBA), the (RETURN) prompts ($1FC3, and $21E8 on the bottom line) and the string at $F4D0 ($056B).
Put back the text bit pointer $31/$32 from the operands save_bit_pointer wrote, so decoding resumes where it stopped.
Operand of LDA #: the low byte of $31 kept by save_bit_pointer ($03 in play-map).
Operand of LDA #: the high byte of $32 kept by save_bit_pointer ($30 in play-map); stored back to $32 by the next instruction.

Bank RAM in everywhere: keeps A in ram_in_saved_a and the processor flags in ram_in_saved_flags, SEI, $01 = $34 (no I/O, no ROM); returns with A unchanged and interrupts off. io_back_in undoes it. Entry $04FC.
Operand of LDA #: the A that all_ram_in was called with, reloaded so the caller gets it back.

Make map $09 the current map $91 unless it is already: save_map writes the old one back, load_map_pages loads the new one to $3400; sets $54 = $13, the height $55 and width $56 both to header byte $2C (every map is square, 32 or 64), $59 = 9, $5A = 4, $D2 = 0; unpack_map_stream fills $DE00-$EDFF; $63 = $FF; header byte $30 names the tile set, unpacked to $D000 by unpack_tile_set when it differs from tile_set_loaded. Ends at $18EA, which writes the game state to T35/L7-L0 of whichever side is then in the drive: always the new map's own, since every map's stream and tile set are on its side (the 42 directory entries, read from the copies). Entry $03B6.

Operand of CMP #: the tile set now unpacked at $D000, $FF at boot (none), written by enter_map before it calls unpack_tile_set; the same set skips the unpack. From here enter_map unpacks the set and ends at $18EA.

Read T35/L8 to $5A00 (read_map_flags); $61/$62 = the map header: $4C00 when byte $09 of that sector is $40, $3A00 when it is not or when $09 is negative. A negative $09 is first replaced by byte $5A00+$09 ($80-$BF give map 5, $C0-$FC map 11 on every side). Then load_dir_entry loads that entry of the map directory T35/L14 to $3400. Leaves $09 = $91.

Load portrait A unless its number (A AND $7F) is already in $0505: returns carry clear then. Bit 7 picks the buffer: set, $E000 with limit $F000; clear, $CA00 with limit $D000, which also sets module_in_memory to $FF. Stores the number in $0505 first, then unpacks that entry of the portrait directory T35/L10 with $AC held at 0 and $09 kept; carry set. Called from $0561 and $05CF.

Operand of LDA #: load_portrait's A as passed, bit 7 included; the BMI after it chooses the $E000 buffer. From here to $267B: set destination and limit, unpack entry $0505 of T35/L10 with $09 and $AC kept.
Set the unpack destination: $FE/$FF and its copy $B9/$BA = X (low), Y (high). The portrait code reads the portrait through ($B9) ($0588) and set_unpack_limit counts from it.
Set the unpack limit $CC/$CD to $B9/$BA plus A pages: A = 6 gives $CA00-$CFFF, A = $10 gives $E000-$EFFF.

Unpack module A, entry A of the directory at T34/L16, to $CA00 with limit $D000 ($09 kept), then mark the portrait $0505 as gone ($FF). It skips the load when A equals module_in_memory, but no code found stores a module number there, so every call loads. Entry $03BF.
Byte load_module compares A with to skip a load. $FF at boot and in every snapshot taken; the only store found is $FF, by load_portrait ($2644), so the skip never happens for modules 0-4.

Load file $75 of the directory at T35/L15 to $3100 (point_at_item_tables, load_dir_entry, $09 kept) unless $76, the file now there, already equals $75; sets $76 = $75. The directory names four 3-page files: entries 0 and 1 on side 1, 2 on side 2, 4 on side 4. Entry $03BC.
Write $3100 back to its file, entry $76 of the directory at T35/L15: point_at_item_tables, then save_dir_entry with $91 swapped for $76 during the call. Entry $03C2.

Unpack the map stream, entry $09 of the directory at T35/L13 (a negative $09 translated through T35/L8 as in load_map_pages), to $DE00 with limit $EE00, all RAM banked in meanwhile. First marks the portrait $0505 gone if the portrait buffer page $BA is $DE. Leaves $09 = $91. Entry $03C5.

Unpack tile set $09, entry $09 of the directory at T35/L12, to $D000 with limit $DE00, all RAM banked in; the 128 bytes at $DD80-$DDFF (engine code under I/O) are pushed on the stack before and written back after, over whatever the unpack put there. Falls into io_back_in.
Bank I/O back in ($01 = $35) and restore the processor flags all_ram_in saved, so interrupts are on again only if they were; A unchanged. Entry $04FF.
Operand of LDA #: the processor flags all_ram_in pushed and stored; io_back_in pushes them and PLP restores the interrupt flag.

Unpack entry $09 of a packed-stream directory at logical sector X, track Y: read_dir_entry gives the start byte ($10), the sector count from the base ($11) and a third byte (to $CE), and checks the side; steps $11 sectors on from the base track/sector in the directory's last two bytes ($5AFE/$5AFF) with $FD0B, reads that sector to $5A00 ($FD19) and jumps to the unpacker $0524 with A = start byte, X/Y = the destination $FE/$FF had on entry. Limit in $CC/$CD.
Operand of LDA #: the entry's first byte, the offset of the packed data in its first sector, passed to $0524 in A.
Operand of LDX #: the low byte of $FE on entry to unpack_entry, passed to $0524 in X.
Operand of LDY #: the high byte of $FF on entry to unpack_entry, passed to $0524 in Y; JMP $0524 follows.

Read entry A of a directory of four-byte entries at track Y, logical sector X (an entry from $40 up is entry AND $3F of the next sector): reads the sector to $5A00, asks for the side in the entry's fourth byte ($1897 returns once that side is in), reads the sector again from that side, and returns $10 = byte 0, $11 = byte 1, A = byte 2. $FE/$FF kept. Every side carries every directory, but an entry holds its data only on the sides that store the file and elsewhere just the side to ask for, hence the second read; a file stored on several sides (module 0, portraits 0 and 8 on all four) comes from the disk in the drive when it has a copy.
Operand of LDA #: the entry number read_dir_entry was called with; times four (ASL ASL) it indexes the sector at $5A00, so $40 and up wrap.
Operand of LDA #: the entry's fourth byte, the disk side, passed to $1897 until that side is in; then the sector is read again and the entry's bytes returned.
Read the directory sector to $5A00 through $FD1D: dir_sector and dir_track, its own LDX/LDY operands, are written by read_dir_entry.
Operand of LDX #: the directory's logical sector, written by read_dir_entry (13, T35/L13, in play-map).
Operand of LDY #: the directory's track, written by read_dir_entry ($23 = 35 in play-map); JMP $FD1D follows.

The engine's disk call, with retry: A = loader operation (0 read one sector, 1 read up to page $FD, 2 write one sector), X = logical sector, Y = track, $FE/$FF the memory; JSR $FC00 (JMP $FF00).
