On an error: keeps $23-$28, prints $A4 "I/O ERROR", or $A5 "Write protected" when the status $FC is $2B, then $A7 ". (RETURN)" on row 23, waits (wait_return), redraws the menu ($1B36), puts $FE/$FF/$FD back and tries again; back-arrow does not cancel. Entry $03AA.
Operand of LDX #: disk_io's logical sector, kept here so the retry at $2800 repeats the call.
Operand of LDY #: disk_io's track, kept for the retry.
Operand of LDA #: disk_io's loader operation, kept for the retry; then JSR $FC00 and, on carry set, the error message and retry from $280C.
Operand of LDA #: $FE as disk_io found it, put back before the retry; the error path ends here, restoring $FE, $FF, $FD and jumping back to $2800.
Operand of LDA #: $FF as disk_io found it, put back before the retry.
Operand of LDA #: $FD (the loader's last page) as disk_io found it, put back before the retry; JMP $2800 follows.
Load the file of entry $09 of the directory at logical sector X, track Y: read_dir_entry gives its track, sector and page count, read_pages loads it to ($FE).
Read A pages to ($FE) from track Y, logical sector X on: $FD = $FF + A - 1, the last page, then disk_io with operation 1. Entry $03B0; the unpacker $0524 swaps the page at $C800 this way.

Write the current map back: nothing when $91 is negative, which is $FF (no map) or a number from $80 up that load_map_pages translated to map 5 or 11, so a map entered that way is never written back; otherwise point_at_maps and save_dir_entry write $3400 on to the sectors of entry $91 of the map directory T35/L14. Entry $03B9.
Write ($FE) back to the file of entry $91 of the directory at logical sector X, track Y: read_dir_entry gives track, sector and page count, then write_pages.

Write A pages from ($FE) to track Y, logical sector X on: one disk_io call with operation 2 per page, the count in $029B, track and sector kept in write_track/write_sector and stepped with $FD0B, $FF stepped by one. Returns carry clear. Entry $03B3.
Operand of LDX #: write_pages' current logical sector; the loop from here writes a page, steps sector and track with $FD0B and counts $029B down.
Operand of LDY #: write_pages' current track, stepped with the sector by $FD0B.

Load and start a program at track $10, logical sector $11: sets the menu table $3E/$3F to load_menu_table and menu $3B = 0, reads the first sector to $5A00 ($FD19), takes the load address from +3/+4 and the page count from +5, reads the whole program from that sector to there (disk_io, operation 1) and JMP ($5A03). Entry $03AD.

Menu table that load_program puts in $3E/$3F while a program loads: one pointer, to load_menu_text. $1B36 redraws the bottom line from ($3E) indexed by menu $3B*2, so a disk error during the load finds an empty menu here, not the program being overwritten.
The empty menu: $03 (printer control 3, clear to the end of the line) and the 0 that ends the string.
Set $FE/$FF = $3100 and X = $0F, Y = $23: the directory of item tables, track 35 logical sector 15.
Set $FE/$FF = $3400 and X = $0E, Y = $23: the map directory, track 35 logical sector 14.
Read track 35, logical sector 8 to $5A00 through $FD1D: per-map bytes $00-$7F ($40 or $20), the map number translations $80-$FC, the disk identity in $FD-$FF.
Start reading a text block: $31/$32 = $52/$53 + $3C, the block's table of group offsets, and $6C = $FF so that the next text_bits fetches a fresh byte. Entry $03D7; $1E0E calls it to find message n.

Decode one character from the bit stream at ($31) through the alphabet at ($52): code $1E sets the capital flag (bit 7 of $6D, tested as bit 6 after the LSR) and reads on; $1F reads one more code and adds $1E; a lower-case result ($61-$FA) after $1E has $20 taken off. Returns A = the character, 0 at the end of a message; Y = the code. Entry $03DA.

Read five bits from the packed text, lowest bit first: $6E holds the byte being shifted out and $6C counts its bits down (negative: fetch the next byte from ($31) and step $31/$32, X = 7). Returns the code in A bits 0-4, Y = 0.

The interrupt handler (IRQ vector $FFFE -> $04F9 -> here): pushes A, X, Y and $01, sets $01 = $35 so I/O is visible, LSR $D019 acknowledges the raster interrupt and moves its flag into carry; if it was set, scan_keyboard. Reads $DC0D to clear CIA 1's interrupt, puts $01, Y, X, A back, RTI.
RTI: the NMI handler (vector $FFFA -> $04F6 -> here), so RESTORE does nothing.

Keyboard scan, from the raster interrupt: if no key is down ($DC00 = 0, $DC01 = $FF) every key_row_state becomes $FF. Otherwise reads each row (pattern in key_row_pattern), twice until stable, ORed with key_row_masks. A row that changes back to $FF is reset; a row that changes while it held no key stores its bits, and its first key from column 7 down gives index 8*(7-row)+(7-column) into the 64-byte table at $C953; a code with bit 7 set goes to $EC. One key per call.

Operand of LDA #: the row select for $DC00, $FE for row 0 (X = 7), rotated left with carry set after each row ($29A3). The loop from here reads, debounces, masks and compares each row, and registers a new key ($29BD).
Operand of LDA #: the new column bits of the row being registered (written at $29B3); stored as its key_row_state, then shifted left to find the first key down.

Masks ORed into the column bits, indexed by X = 7 - row: $04 for row 7 (CTRL), $10 for row 6 (right SHIFT), $80 for row 1 (left SHIFT), 0 elsewhere. The scan never registers those three keys and has no shifted codes.
Last column bits accepted for each row, indexed by X = 7 - row; $FF when the row has no key down (all eight in play-map). scan_keyboard takes a new key only from a row whose state was $FF.

The engine text block, base $29E4 (the word at $0200 points here; $0519 puts it in $43/$44). Its 60-byte alphabet, code -> byte: 00 {0A}, 01 s, 02 end, 03 space, 04 e, 05 a, 06 r, 07 o, 08 i, 09 t, 0A n, 0B l, 0C c, 0D m, 0E p, 0F d, 10 u, 11 h, 12 k, 13 newline, 14 f, 15 g, 16 b, 17 y, 18 w, 19 v, 1A 1, 1B ., 1C x, 1D 9, 1E ), 1F j, 20 7, 21 {0B}, 22 {03}, 23 {02}, 24 z, 25 {06}, 26 {04}, 27 {01}, 28 ', 29 q, 2A ?, 2B :, 2C /, 2D (, 2E {0C}, 2F {07}, 30 8, 31 5, 32 4, 33 2, 34 -, 35 {7F}, 36 | (inverted Y), 37 6, 38 3, 39 #, 3A {08}, 3B {7F}. Codes $1E (capital) and $1F (escape: next code + $1E) never index it directly. Bytes below $10 are printer controls (table at $1F42): {01}/{02} set/clear $29, {03} clears to the line end, {04} clears the window, {06} prints (RETURN) and waits, {0A}a{0A}b{0A} prints a for a count $38 of 1 and b otherwise, {0B} prints a name ($173A), {0C}a{0C}b{0C} chooses by $BB (his/her), {0D} new line.

The sector buffer, one page: read_sector_xy and read_sector_10_11 read each single sector here (directories, program headers, the side identity, packed streams as they unpack), so what it holds is the last sector read; in play-map it holds stream data. Layouts by sector: a directory, four-byte entries (track, logical sector, count or pages, side; in a stream directory the first two are the start byte and the sector count from the base at $5AFE/$5AFF; $27CD-$27DD); T35/L8, one byte per map number ($40 tested at $260D; for a map number with bit 7 set, the real number, $2621) and the identity at $5AFD-$5AFF. Borrowed as work space: the engine holds part of a character record in its first 60 bytes ($1005-$103A, $13B7-$13DE, $1440); the game's melee_round builds its initiative list here, a 16-bit value in each two-byte slot ($7F72-$8063, $823A-$8252), and range_target a table of 21 three-byte entries, distance, base value and base + 7 ($BD5C-$BD90); the Ranger Center copies a new character's name here to compare it with the others ($81D4). It is also the buffer of typed lines: the Ranger Center's names ($8364-$836C, 13 characters), the game's answers to a question square ($8927-$8931, 16; a one-key answer is stored as a one-character string, $8913-$891A), each compared with the answer messages the game decodes to $5A80 ($895A, $8964-$8974), and map 13's 13-character name for a cloned character ($42BB-$42D9 in map-13.vsf). The uses outside the engine come from the other parts' names.

Byte 1 of the sector buffer: a directory entry's logical sector, or in a stream directory its sector count from the base ($5A01,Y at $27D2, to $11); the second byte of a slot of the game's initiative list ($823E, $8252, read at $8063) and of an entry of range_target's table ($BD65).
Byte 2 of the sector buffer: a directory entry's third byte, its page count or stream count ($5A02,Y at $27DD); the third byte of an entry of the game's range_target table ($BD6E).

A program header's load address, low byte (high at $5A04), read by load_program ($289F) into $FE and jumped through at $28BA (JMP ($5A03)); in a directory, entry 0's side byte ($5A03,Y at $27BB, passed to the side check at $1897).
High byte of a program header's load address, read at $28A4 into $FF.
A program header's page count, added to the load page at $28AA to give the last page ($FD) for the load.

In T35/L8, the first byte of the side's identity: $00 on a play disk, $D7 on a master; the side check at $18AB wants it equal to $ED (0 in play), which is how masters are refused. The utility program reads T35/L8 itself (loader call at $807E-$8080) and wants a master there: $D7, $CC and its side number from $7F8C ($808D-$80A1).
In T35/L8, the identity's middle byte, always $CC (checked at $18B5). In a stream directory (T35/L13, L12, L10, T34/L16) the base track the entries count from ($276F).
In T35/L8, the side number (1-4) the side check compares with $6B ($18B9). In a stream directory, the base logical sector ($2772).

This first table: 79 pronoun classes, 0 he/him, 1 she/her, 2 it, read only at the game's $9EBC with Y = byte 7 of an eight-byte record ($16, found by monster_record $9EA4, which $9E9F falls into, through $039E) into $CA, which the text filter at $20C3 uses to keep one of three {0E}-separated forms, as in the game's '{0E}he{0E}she{0E}it{0E}' (message 34). Byte 7 of a monster's record is also the picture encounter_portrait shows (game $B965: $9EDE, then show_picture $0419 at $B99D), so each pronoun goes with a picture.

Sixteen four-byte records, four per party (party n's at $5B4F + 16n, the game's party_record_block $98BC): the column, row and map of an encounter square (class 3 or 15) for which the party is the nearest that can engage, and its distance from the party, 10 a square (store_position_record $97F2: $983F, $9841, $09, $9672), or a party number 0-3 when the square already had a record ($963C-$9652; see $5B52). scan_for_encounters wipes all 16 ($94D4-$94DC) and fills them anew. When the party's four records are full, a nearer square replaces the first of them that is farther away, not the farthest ($9671-$967D, $96E3-$96F0); when none is, the next nearest party is tried ($967F-$9687, $96F2-$96FA). clear_position_record ($980F) frees one; find_position_record ($9843) searches them by column, row and map, and find_group_at_record ($9877) searches the battle groups of parties 0-3 for the one at a record's column, row and map. Byte 0 = 0 marks a free record; all free in both snapshots. From the game part's use.
Second byte (y) of each position_records entry, as $5B50,Y or $5B50,X ($9390, $97FB, $9892).
Third byte of each position_records entry, the map number from $09 ($9800), compared at $9860 and $989A.

Fourth byte of each position_records entry: the square's distance from the party, 10 a square ($9672, stored at $9806), when the record is made for a square that had none ($96C1); for a square that already had one, $9649 loads the party chosen in an earlier pass ($964A) and $964F stores it in $9672, so the byte is a party number, 0-3. $96E6 compares a new square's distance with it, and $9673, for a square that already had a record, that party number, record by record: the first record that holds a larger one is replaced.

Top logical sector for a file that steps down onto a track, read by next_logical_sector as LDA $C930,X with X = the new, lower track ($FD14): 35 bytes, tracks 0-16 20, 17 0, 18-23 18, 24-29 17, 30-34 16. Apart from track 17's 0, each value is the top sector of the track one higher (zones of 21, 19, 18 and 17 sectors give 20, 18, 17 and 16), so it is right inside a speed zone and wrong where a file crosses into the next zone: a file running from track 25 into 24 continues at sector 17 (track 24's sector 18 is never reached that way), from 31 into 30 at 16 (sector 17 never reached), and from 19 into 17 (18 skipped) at sector 0 only, then on to track 16 at sector 20. Writes step through the same routine, so the disks are consistent with it: the game program (T31/L9, 72 pages, down to track 27) matches the loaded $7E00-$C5FF byte for byte only when read this way, and so do all 42 maps as enter_map loads them.

Key codes for scan_keyboard ($29CC): 64 entries indexed 8 * (7 - row) + (7 - column) of the keyboard matrix (row = the $DC00 line driven low, column = the $DC01 bit read low), the reverse of the KERNAL's numbering. ASCII + $80: capitals A-Z, digits, punctuation, SPACE $A0, RETURN $8D, DEL $88, CRSR right $95, CRSR down $8A, F1 F3 F5 F7 $F1 $F3 $F5 $F7, left arrow $9B, RUN/STOP $98, and C= $95 like CRSR right. $00 (ignored, bit 7 clear) for both SHIFTs, CTRL, pound, HOME and up arrow. There is no second, shifted table: the scan masks both SHIFTs and CTRL out ($29D4) before indexing.

Plays sound X on SID voice 1: control $D404 = 0 (gate off), volume $D418 = $0F, then record X of sound_table: seven bytes to $D406 down to $D400 (sustain/release, attack/decay, control, pulse width high and low, frequency high and low), three to $D417 down to $D415 (filter registers; no voice routed through it) and the last to $D404, the control byte that starts the note when its gate bit is set. X = 0 explosion (screen_shake, $0748; entry $044C, called by module 4 at $CA4C and by the code of maps 3, 4, 9, 12, 18, 20, 27, 31, 33, 35, 36 and 39, and the use effect 1 of item_effect), 11 ($241C, through $0232; its final control byte $A4 has the gate bit clear, so as written it starts no note), 22 ($0741, through $04D2).

Three 11-byte records for play_sound, at offsets 0, 11 and 22 (layout: $D406, $D405, $D404, $D403, $D402, $D401, $D400, $D417, $D416, $D415, then $D404 again). 0: noise at frequency $2000, attack 1, decay $A, sustain 0, gate on ($85): the explosion. 11: frequency $2000, pulse width $06A4, sustain 6, release 0, but its final control byte $A4 has the gate bit clear, so as written it starts no note; it is called through $0232 by the game ($92BC), the Ranger Center ($8188) and modules 1 ($CC2D, $CC52) and 2 ($CAB5). 22: noise at $1000, attack, decay and sustain 0, gate on ($81): a click, sounded through $04D2 by the game's main loop ($7E84), after every move that succeeds and every left-arrow step in place (game $AE26, reached from I, J, L and K at $AE1E, $AE4B, $AE6A and $AE89 and from left-arrow at $AE21, which the game's start also calls when $92 is set, $7E60) and by the start-up ($8427).

35 bytes after the last sound record ($C9DD-$C9FF) that no instruction in any part reads (operand scan of every part's snapshot, and play_sound only takes offsets 0, 11 and 22). $C9E0-$C9E7 has the shape of a glyph, a bracket in %01, where glyph $9C would be; no caller passes that code. Loaded with the font's last page (T34/L11); $C9DD-$C9DE hold $14 $15 and the rest is zero.

Copies one character row of the map window for the game's scrolls ($BE26 picture left, $BE44 right, $BE74 up, $BE90 down). It lies in RAM under the I/O area, so it runs only while the game has the I/O banked out ($01 = $34, all_ram_in through $04FC at $BECC). First the row's screen-matrix colours: LDA source,Y / STA destination,X, both addresses, the start indexes, the CPY end and the INX/INY or DEX/DEY steps patched in by the game ($BECC from scroll_matrix_*, $BEEE and $BF0F from screen_row_address $0502). Then the bitmap: $20 groups of eight bytes from ($12) to ($14) (copy_cells), $13/$15 stepped a page, and 2 or 4 more groups (the LDX operand at $DD9C, patched at $BE4B and $BEC0): 272 bytes (34 cells) for a sideways scroll, 288 (36) for an upright one. unpack_tile_set pushes these 128 bytes on the stack and pulls them back around a tile-set unpack ($2727, $2748), whose limit of $DE00 ($273A) would let the tile set run over them.
Operand of the LDY #$00 at $DD90: the first index of the bitmap copy, patched by set_copy_direction ($00 forward, $FF backward).
Opcode byte patched by set_copy_direction: INC $13 ($E6) or DEC $13 ($C6), moving the bitmap source a page on or back after the first 256 bytes.
Opcode byte patched like scroll_src_page_step: INC $15 or DEC $15, the destination's page step.

Copies X groups of eight bytes from ($12),Y to ($14),Y. The step after each byte is one of eight slots ($DDA1 + 5n) that set_copy_direction fills with INY or DEY, so a group runs up or down through the page and Y wraps within it.
First of copy_cells' eight step slots, every fifth byte from here to $DDC4: INY ($C8) for a forward copy, DEY ($88) for a backward one, written by set_copy_direction.

Sets the direction of scroll_copy_row's bitmap copy: Y = first index (to $DD91), X = INC or DEC zero-page opcode (to $DD97 and $DD99), A = INY or DEY opcode (to the eight slots from $DDA1, five bytes apart). The game calls it with the I/O banked out: $BE54 backward (Y = $FF, DEC, DEY) for the picture moving right, $BEC9 forward (Y = 0, INC, INY) for the other three.
Start index of the colour copy's source for the game's scroll kinds X = 0 picture left, 1 picture right, 2 up or down (the game's $BECC puts it in $DD81): 3, 34, 1.
Source step of the colour copy for X = 0-2, an opcode for $DD8B: INY, DEY, INY ($C8, $88, $C8).
End of the colour copy for X = 0-2, the CPY operand at $DD8D: 36, 1, 37; so columns 3-35 go to 1-33, 34 down to 2 go to 36 down to 4, and 1-36 to 1-36 of another row.
Start index of the colour copy's destination for X = 0-2 (to $DD83): 1, 36, 1.
Destination step for X = 0-2, an opcode for $DD8A: INX, DEX, INX ($E8, $CA, $E8).
Low bytes 8 and 40 of the offset the game's $BEEE (X = 0) and $BEF0 (X = 1) add to a row's bitmap address for the destination ($14): cell 1 or cell 5 of the row.
High bytes of scroll_bitmap_dst_offset, both 0 (added into $15).
Low bytes 24 and 8 of the offset the game's $BF0F (X = 0, cell 3) and $BF12 (X = 1, cell 1; reached through the BIT skip at $BF11) add to a row's bitmap address for the source ($12).
High bytes of scroll_bitmap_src_offset, both 0 (added into $13).
Five zero bytes ending the 128 the boot file copies to $DD80; nothing reads them except the engine's save and restore of the whole stretch ($2727, $2748).

Encounter groups, used only by the game through group_ptr $79/$7A: for each party 0-3, four groups of 94 bytes at $EE00 + 376*party + 94*group (the game's $BBC7, A = party, X = group), which fills $EE00-$F3DF exactly. A group is a 4-byte head, +0/+1 its map column and row (+0 = 0: no group, $83FE), +2 its map ($B692), +3 its distance in feet from the party, measured at each scan ($9413-$9418, $BAEC), then three 30-byte lines at +4 + 30*line ($BB9F; the game's line_index $BD9A numbers all 48 lines (4*party + group)*3 + line). A line holds ten 16-bit hit points, one per monster, 0 for a dead one (+$00-$13, $A83C), then ten flag bytes (+$14-$1D, $BB35). Not part of the saved game, which starts at $F400; the start-up clears $EE00-$F3FF, six pages, after zero page ($7F3D-$7F53). The picture buffer at $E000 (show_picture_e000, entry $041C, limit $F000) covers $EE00-$EFFF too, and modules 0-2, which show their pictures there, restore only the map stream below $EE00 (unpack_map_stream at module-0 $CA55, module-1 $CA93, module-2 $CA46). From the game part's use.

Four bytes, one per party 0-3, used only by the game: encounter_party_distances ($977E) stores each party's distance to the square the encounter scan is on ($983F/$9841), 10 a square from the engine's table at $0921 (entry $04CF), or $FF when the party does not exist, has nobody conscious, is on another map, has the square outside its view ($B119), cannot see it ($8347), or is farther than both the encounter record's byte 1 at ($77) and its own reach, party_reach ($F4E1). nearest_engaging_party ($97D8) picks the smallest; $9684 and $96F7 set a party's entry to $FF when none of its four position records ($5B4F) holds a farther square, and $9684 also when that party already holds the square's record ($9689-$968F), so the next nearest is tried. Zero in play-map. From the game part's use.

Eight flags, one per party position (1-7 used), read only by the game's print_flagged_names ($BCF6): it prints the names of the flagged members, separated by ', ' (character $2C through $0284) and joined by ' and ' before the last (message 45, $ABB6), $BD0A-$BD45. The only setter clears all eight and flags positions 1-$07, the whole party ($A33C-$A34D), before '... move.' (message 92, $A353-$A358). From the game part's use.

Sixteen bytes, one per encounter group, index party*4 + group, used only by the game: the groups' move plans for a battle round. plan_group_moves sets all to $FF, no plan ($83D7-$83E1), and stores the plan of each hostile group that can move at $856D: a direction 0-8 in bits 0-5 (the numbering of direction_by_cell $5BE3) and the kind in bits 6-7, 0 a better square, 1 flee ($40), 2 close in ($80). move_groups ($872D) carries them out, splitting kind and direction ($87CA, $87EF); melee_round's hit chance is higher against a group with a plan ($80E7 tests for $FF). $F3FC-$F3FF after them: no reference found. From the game part's use (its names).

Page 0 of the saved game ($F400-$FBFF, eight pages written to T35/L7 down to L0 by save_game), starting with the four party tables, 14 bytes each at $F400, $F40E, $F41C and $F42A (party_table_ptr $1768, party_table_offsets $1778). In a table, +1 to +7 are the record numbers of positions 1-7 (0 for none), +8/+9 the party's map column and row, +10 its map (game $9C17-$9C55), +11/+12/+13 the column, row and map it last left by an exit (game $89BA-$89D7), to which an exit whose map byte is $FF takes it back ($89DD-$89FD); +0 has no use found. In play-map party 0 holds records 1-4 at column 55, row 62 of map 0.

Saved page 0, $F438-$F477: four 16-byte blocks, one per party at $F438 + 16*party (order_table_offsets $BCDD), used only by the game: eight order bytes, one per party position, where order_tables_ptr points $89/$8A, then eight parameter bytes ($8B/$8C): the combat orders of an encounter round, numbered 0-8 as the game's order_keys index them (see $89 and $8B). The orders are cleared after each round ($A2B8; all eight at $A36A-$A371 after a party move, which a blocked square or a party with nobody conscious skips, leaving the mover's order and those after it, $A326-$A330) and before a party is asked again ($B3B2); the parameters are left as they were. In play-map party 0's orders are 0 and the other bytes are as the saved game on the disk images holds them (T35/L7, unscrambled). Saved with the game.

Copy of zero page $02-$0F in the saved game (14 bytes, $F478-$F485): save_game copies them here before it writes the pages ($18EC-$18F2), and the start-up and utils copy them back after loading a save (start-up $8350, utils $80EE). So the view position, the elapsed count, the party counts, the map, the clock and the scroll speed travel with the save. In play-map the copy is behind the live values: $04 $10 against $40, minutes 12 against 24.

Used only by the game: the fight routine encounter ($B1A3, run by Enc and by encounter_if_engaged $B197) stores $0A, the records in use, at $F486 and the 24-bit experience of records 1-7 (exp_load, entry $038C) in three bytes each from $F487 ($B1AD-$B1D4, up to $F49B). When the encounter ends, $B32E-$B374 subtracts these from each record's experience and prints '<name> gains n experience.' (messages 39 and 40) for every record up to the count with a non-zero gain. Saved with the game.

Line buffer of the word-wrapped output, one byte per screen column (41 bytes, $F49C-$F4C4), each character less $20 so that 0 is a space where a line may break ($1FEB, $2015): buffer_char puts each character at its column ($1FEF), draw_buffered_line finds the break column (break_column_op $202F), draws the line and carries the cut word over ($2012-$2055), clear_line_buffer zeroes it ($22CF). It lies inside saved page 0, so the start-up and utils clear it after loading a save ($835B, $80F9 call $04ED). The game also prints into it for the picture caption: encounter_portrait turns the output back on ($B94B, $B940) and prints the name word-wrapped without ending the line, so nothing is drawn, then copies the buffer out ($B98D). $F4C5-$F4CF after it: no reference found in any part's code; play-map holds 00 EF B2 00 B0 00 B0 00 B0 00 00 there, carried in the save.

Caption under the picture window: a zero-ended string of up to 11 characters in the 12 bytes $F4D0-$F4DB, except where all 12 are characters, as in the death screen's 'Grim Reaper ', which ends at the zero in $F4DC. draw_picture_window prints it at column 1, row 13 ($0571-$057D). The game builds it centred from what it printed into the line buffer ($B960-$B99A: eleven spaces, the zero at $F4DB, then the text). Modules 0-3 copy the location's name into it, 12 bytes of the square's record at ($5F): module 0 (the doctor) and module 1 (the shop) from byte 7 ($CA06-$CA13, $CA0F-$CA1C), module 2 (the library) from byte 4 and module 3 (the way into the Ranger Center) from byte 3 ($CA06-$CA13 in both); module 3's is the caption the Ranger Center shows. The radio program (from its $8184, $7EAA-$7EB5) and the death screen (from its $7E2F, $7E06-$7E11) copy in captions of their own; module 4 empties it with a zero ($CA87-$CA89). The STA $F4D0,X at start-up $8C0B and at ranger $86AF never run: the first is in the copy of the death program that the title picture overwrites, the second in the Ranger Center's copy of the radio program. 'Ranger Ctr.' in play-map.

Zero ending the picture caption, written by the game after it fills $F4D0-$F4DA with spaces ($B973-$B974); the other parts' 12-byte copies include it, except the death screen's, which puts the space of 'Grim Reaper ' here, so its caption ends at $F4DC. $F4DC: no instruction addresses it, but the caption print reads it through $31/$32 ($0571-$057D) whenever $F4DB is not zero; 0 in both death snapshots and in the save on the disk images.

Four bytes, one per party, used only by the fight routine encounter ($B1A3; Enc and encounter_if_engaged): cleared at the start of every round (encounter_round $B1E7-$B1EF, entered again from $B3AC); encounter then works through the parties still at 0 ($B1F5), and after each one sets 1 for every party whose map is $8D ($B2F6-$B314). From the game part's use.

Four bytes, one per party, used only by the game: the longest reach in feet of the party's members (0, 15 or $FE; see $7D). scan_for_encounters calls member_reach ($BC39) for each member and keeps the largest in the operand of its own CMP at $9510, zeroed at $94EE and raised at $9514, then stores it here ($94EC-$951E); a party number above $0B gets 0. In play-map that CMP shows #$FE: the last maximum, not a constant. encounter_party_distances ($97C2) and $9620 compare a square's distance with it after byte 1 of the square's record at ($77): a party with a loaded gun reaches every square it can see, one with only melee weapons the squares around it. From the game part's use.

Twenty bytes the stream unpacker (loaded at $C800 from T35/L16 while a stream unpacks) reads from the start of each packed stream ($C814-$C81D) and uses as its table of frequent bytes: a short code picks entry Y (LDA $F4E5,Y at $C883; the codes are matched against $C8EC). They sit inside saved page 0, so every save carries the table of the last stream unpacked; nothing else reads them.

Base Cochise's self-destruct countdown is armed: 0 or 1. Map 20's own code arms it (map-20.vsf $406B-$4088, entry 4 of its code table at $4013): it copies the elapsed count $04-$06 to countdown_start $F4FA-$F4FC, stores 1 here ($407A-$407C), clears its header byte +$2F and sets off two explosions (screen_shake, $044C). Its messages are the base's ('ALERT! Self destruction sequence activated', 'The screen shows a clock counting down. It shows ...'), and its $408B-$40F7 shows the time left as h:mm.ss from 240 - (count - start), four units a minute. The game checks on every main-loop pass ($7ED2 calls $82B5): when this is set and the count is $F0 or more past the start, it writes the map back (save_map $03B9) and runs module 4, the destruction (LDA #$84 / JMP $8845, $82B5-$82DC), which clears this byte ($CBBC). Map 20's header gives a quarter minute (+$34 = $40) and one count (+$36 = 1) per step, so the 240 units are 240 steps, one game hour, a minute every four steps. 0 in play-map.

Low byte of the elapsed count ($04) when the countdown was armed: stored by map 20's code (map-20.vsf $406B-$406D), subtracted by the game's check ($82BD) and by map 20's clock ($408E). play-map holds $38 $8E $00 at $F4FA-$F4FC with the countdown off, carried in the save.
Middle byte of the countdown's start count ($05): map 20 stores it ($4072), the game ($82C3) and map 20 ($4096) subtract it.
High byte of the countdown's start count ($06): map 20 stores it ($4077), the game subtracts it ($82C9).

Top byte of the 32-bit elapsed count $04-$06: raised when $06 carries (game $AF72). The start-up's and utils' search for the latest save compares it last ($824F, $8265; utils $81DB, $81F1), and map 13's code keeps 32-bit time stamps of the count and waits for $2D00 units to pass (map-13.vsf $3E27-$3E39, $4258-$4283). $F4FE: no reference found.

Checksum of the saved game and the key of its scrambling: save_game stores save_checksum's result here ($18FA) before scramble_save EORs bytes 0-$FE of every page with 2*offset EOR this byte; byte $FF of each page, this one included, stays in clear. The start-up and utils unscramble a loaded save with it and compare the checksum ($8321-$832A; utils $80BF-$80C8). On a mismatch they EOR every page with 2*offset once more and carry on ($832F-$834C; utils $80CD-$80EA): with a key of 0 the two passes cancel, so a save stored in clear with 0 here loads as it is. $C7 in play-map.

Character records 1-7, 256 bytes each at $F400 + 256 * record (record 1 here; pages 1-7 of the saved game). The engine's fields are listed at $66. The other programs add, each checked in their code: +$1B/+$1C the maximum CON (health_tick $B7E9-$B7FB); +$1F the equipped slot, as (its item offset - $BB) / 2 (game $A569, $A57A-$A581); +$26/+$27 the CON before the blow that downed the member, half of which it wakes with (game $A934, $B7C2-$B7D2); +$28 afflictions: with any of bits 4-7 set the member loses a point of CON every 64 time units, two while down, and any non-zero value stops healing and waking (game $B7A2-$B7A8, $B816-$B853, $B854); +$2B-+$2E an NPC's refusal bytes, tested by the engine's willingness check ($0D61; +$2E for a trade) and lowered after a good hire (game $A4A4-$A4AE); +$30 an NPC's message on joining (game $A484); +$31 an NPC's hire difficulty, 0 joining at once (game $A43E), set to the hirer's CHR (+$14) when it joins ($A490-$A494, the operand written at $A406); +$32 on the rank's name, zero-ended (radio $81BC-$81CC, ranger $8005-$8012); +$4B bit 0 Base Cochise destroyed, set in every record by module 4 ($CA03-$CA1C) and read by the radio ($7EC9); +$4C bit 0 the radio has given the reward for it ($7ED1-$7EDD). Bits 0-3 of +$28 are diseases as well: the doctor lists bit n as message n + 1 of its text (module 0, $CC04-$CC28), 0 Radiation poisoning (set by a radiation square, game $8313-$831C), 1 Wasteland Herpes, 2 Bug byte, 3 Sewer rot, and 4-7 Desert dust, Rabies, D6 and D7.

Page 7 of the saved game, character record 7 ($FB00-$FBFF; records 1-7 are $F500-$FBFF, $F400 + record*256, all laid out as described at $66). The symbol comes from loader_main's STA $FB00,X and LDA $FB00,X ($FF34, $FF6C): every loader call sets both operands from $FE/$FF ($FF0F-$FF1A), and in play-map the last call moved this page of the save.

Fast loader's entry as the game calls it (the engine's disk_io JSR at $2806, the utility program at $7F73, $7FB4, $8080): JMP loader_main. Same inputs and results as loader_main: A = command, Y = track, X = logical sector, $FE/$FF buffer, $FD last page; status in $FC, carry set on failure.

264 bytes loader_receive_byte reads as ($F6),Y with Y = the raster line ($D012) and $F6 = 3 + (7 - the vertical scroll), set by loader_send_command, so the pattern follows the scroll: $0F (safe; also the mask that clears bits 4-7 of $DD00) everywhere except $00 on the raster lines whose low three bits equal the scroll, from $30 + scroll on, and on the line before each, where the video chip's character-row fetch would steal cycles from the timed two-bit read. Only the last byte, $FD0A, is past every index: $F6 is at most 10 (a vertical scroll of 0), so with $D012 at $FF the reads reach $FD09.

Steps X = track, Y = logical sector to a file's next sector: Y - 1, or when that goes below 0 the track below (track 18, the directory track, is skipped) at the sector top_sector_of_track_above gives for that lower track ($C930,X at $FD14). Inside a speed zone that is the track's top sector; across a zone boundary it is not: 25 into 24 starts at 17, 31 into 30 at 16, 19 into 17 at 0, below those tracks' real tops (18, 17 and 20). Files run downwards. Called by loader_main between sectors, by the engine's directory and stream code ($2779, $279D, $287E), by the stream unpacker loaded at $C800 ($C8D6) and by the utility program ($8405).

Reads one sector into the sector buffer at $5A00: track from $10, logical sector from $11, then as read_sector_xy. Used for program header sectors (load_program at $289C), a packed stream's first sector ($2784) and, from the unpacker at $C800, its later ones ($C8DD), the side check ($18A6) and module 4 ($CCBD).

Reads one sector, Y = track and X = logical sector, into the sector buffer at $5A00: $FE/$FF = $5A00 and A = 0 (one sector), through the engine's retrying disk call at $03AA. The PHA/PLA of the 0 around setting $FE/$FF has no effect. Entered by JMP from $27E5 (the directory read_dir_entry names; T35/L13 in play-map) and $28DF (T35/L8) and by the start-up at $7FF1.

Sends A to the drive, bit 7 first: waits (interrupts allowed between polls) until bit 6 of $DD00 reads 1, then writes $DD00 once for each bit, bit 5 = the data bit and bit 4 the clock, which changes with every bit (set for bits 7, 5, 3 and 1: $36 or $16; clear for bits 6, 4, 2 and 0: $26 or $06; bits 0-1 keep VIC bank $4000), with NOPs for timing. $F5 is the shift register. Leaves $DD00 = $26 and interrupts enabled.

Starts a disk job: points $F6/$F7 at $FC00 + 3 + (7 - the vertical scroll in $D011 bits 0-2), raster_safe_table plus 7 - the scroll, so the table lines up with this frame's character rows; writes $26 to $DD00 and keeps in $F4 the correction for the bits of $DD00 that carry no data; sends the command $F3, the track $F8 and the physical sector (logical_to_physical) with loader_send_byte, then runs on into loader_release_bus.
Writes $C6 to $DD00: bits 4 and 5 clear, VIC bank $4000 kept. Ends each exchange with the drive; also the tail of loader_send_command.

Receives one byte from the drive into A: waits (interrupts allowed between polls) until raster_safe_table gives a non-zero entry for the current raster line ($D012), so no character-row fetch stretches the timed read; writes that $0F AND $DD00 back to clear bits 4-7 (the start signal), reads $DD00 four times taking two bits (6 and 7) per read, shifted and EORed together, sets bit 5 again, corrects with $F4 and decodes the bit order through receive_decode_table ($FE00).

The RTS ending loader_receive_byte, which is also the base of the zone table logical_to_physical reads as CMP $FDD3,X with X = 4 down to 1: the bytes used are $FDD4-$FDD7; this RTS opcode ($60) would be compared only for a track of 36 or more.

First tracks of the disk's speed zones, read from the end by logical_to_physical: $24, $1F, $19, $12 (36, 31, 25, 18). A track at or above the boundary at $FDD3 + X lowers X: tracks 31-35 zone 0, 25-30 zone 1, 18-24 zone 2, 1-17 zone 3.
Logical to physical sector map for tracks 25-30, 18 sectors: logical n is physical 7n mod 18 (0, 7, 14, 3, 10, 17, ...); zone 1 in zone_table_pointers.
Logical to physical sector map for tracks 18-24, 19 sectors: logical n is physical 8n mod 19 (0, 8, 16, 5, 13, ...); zone 2 in zone_table_pointers.
Three zero bytes after the zone 2 map, before receive_decode_table's page; no instruction reads them.

256-byte bit-order table: loader_receive_byte looks the byte up here as it was assembled from the four reads of $DD00 (after the $F4 correction). Each received bit lands elsewhere: bit 0 becomes bit 7, 1 becomes 5, 2 becomes 6, 3 becomes 4, 4 becomes 3, 5 becomes 1, 6 becomes 2, 7 becomes 0.
receive_decode_table, continued: the entries for assembled bytes $40-$7F.
receive_decode_table, continued: the entries for assembled bytes $80-$BF.
receive_decode_table, continued: the entries for assembled bytes $C0-$FF.

Fast loader, the computer's side: one disk job. A = command (0 read one sector, 1 read sectors until page $FD is filled, 2 write one sector, 3 and up a drive-side command answered by a status byte only; the utility program sends 3 for track 1 at $7F71), Y = track, X = logical sector, $FE/$FF = buffer, patched into the STA at $FF34 and the LDA at $FF6C. Keeps $F3 command, $F8 track, $F9 sector. Runs with $01 = $35 (old value restored on exit) and $34 around each buffer access, so a buffer may lie under the I/O. Sends the job (loader_send_command), moves 256 bytes per sector, reads the drive's status byte into $FC, and on command 1 steps to the next logical sector (next_logical_sector) and page until page $FD is done. Returns A = $FC compared with 1: carry clear only for status 0.
Low byte of the STA $FB00,X operand at $FF34 that stores each received byte, set from $FE at $FF0F.
High byte of that operand: the page being read, set from $FF at $FF17, compared with $FD at $FF4F and stepped at $FF56 between sectors.
Low byte of the LDA $FB00,X operand at $FF6C that fetches each byte to write, set from $FE at $FF12.
High byte of that operand, the page written, set from $FF at $FF1A.

Common exit of loader_main: puts back the memory map it saved on entry ($FF06-$FF08; PLA, STA $01) and returns the drive's status from $FC compared with 1, so carry is clear only for status 0. Reached when a read's status is not 0 ($FF48), after a one-sector read ($FF4D), when command 1 has filled page $FD ($FF54), and after a write or a drive command ($FF84). The platform's predefined symbol KERNAL_RAMTAS names this address, the ROM's jump-table entry; here it is RAM under the KERNAL, which is switched out whenever the loader runs.

Waits for the drive to finish a job: sets bit 5 of $DD00 (bits 0-3 kept), pauses 12 cycles (loader_delay), polls (interrupts allowed between polls) until bit 6 of $DD00 reads 1, then a short delay loop (X = 20). Called before the data of a read and before the status of a write or a command.
Not a variable: the operand's high byte ($DD) of BIT $DD00 at $FFA0 in loader_wait_drive. The symbol comes from BIT $FFA2 at $1B5E, the skip idiom that hides LDX #$FF.
Not a variable: the offset byte ($FD) of the BNE at $FFA8 in loader_wait_drive's delay loop. The symbol comes from BIT $FFA9 at $1213 and $85C1, the skip idiom that hides LDA #$FF.
A lone RTS: the JSR to it at $FF99 is a 12-cycle pause.

Returns in A the physical sector for logical sector $F9 on track $F8: finds the track's speed zone against zone_first_tracks (CMP $FDD3,X with X = 4 down to 1: tracks 31-35 zone 0, 25-30 zone 1, 18-24 zone 2, 1-17 zone 3), patches the operand of LDA $FFE8,Y at $FFC7 with that zone's table from zone_table_pointers and reads entry $F9.
Low byte of the LDA $FFE8,Y operand at $FFC7, patched by logical_to_physical at $FFBC to the track's zone table.
High byte of that operand, patched at $FFC2.

Addresses of the four logical-to-physical sector maps, by zone: $FFE8 (0: tracks 31-35), $FDD8 (1: 25-30), $FDEA (2: 18-24), $FFD3 (3: 1-17). logical_to_physical reads the low bytes as $FFCB,X and the high bytes as $FFCC,X with X = zone * 2.
The high bytes of zone_table_pointers seen from LDA $FFCC,X at $FFBF; the words start at $FFCB.
Logical to physical sector map for tracks 1-17, 21 sectors: logical n is physical 10n mod 21 (0, 10, 20, 9, 19, ...); zone 3 in zone_table_pointers.

Logical to physical sector map for tracks 31-35, 17 sectors: logical n is physical 6n mod 17 (0, 6, 12, 1, 7, ...); zone 0 in zone_table_pointers, and the value the operand at $FFC7 holds in the snapshot. $FFF9, after it, is an unused zero.

The 6510's hardware vectors in RAM, used because play runs with $01 = $35 (KERNAL out): NMI $04F6 (the engine's JMP to an RTI at $2966), RESET $0000 (never used: a reset brings the KERNAL ROM back, whose vector applies), IRQ $04F9 (JMP irq_handler at $2947).
